# BISCS India: full guide text

> Plain-text version of every guide on https://www.biscsindia.com, for AI assistants. Each tool runs in the browser; files are not uploaded.

## Calculate Exact Age from Date of Birth in Years, Months, Days

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/calculate-exact-age-from-date-of-birth/
Tool: Age Calculator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/)

Quick answer: To calculate exact age, count the completed years since the date of birth, then the completed months after the last birthday, then the remaining days. BISCS India's free Age Calculator does this for any “age as on” date, and also shows total days, weeks and a countdown to your next birthday.

Your exact age is the number of completed years since your date of birth, plus the completed months since your last birthday, plus the leftover days. Someone born on 15 August 1995 is 31 years, 2 months and 18 days old on 2 November 2026.

Doing this by hand is easy to get wrong, because months have different lengths and leap years add a day. The free [Age Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/) handles both, and lets you choose any "age as on" date, which is what most Indian forms actually ask for.

## Why "age as on" a date matters in India

Many forms do not ask how old you are today. They ask your age on a specific cut-off date:

- **Government recruitment** notices usually fix a date, often the first day of a month in the exam year, and set minimum and maximum ages on that date.
- **School admissions** set a minimum age for nursery or Class 1, measured on a cut-off date that varies by state and school board.
- **Insurance and pension** forms may need your age on the policy or joining date.
- **Senior citizen benefits**, such as certain bank deposit rates and income tax slabs, generally begin at age 60.

Being one day short of a limit can make an application invalid. That is why the calculator has a separate "Age on" field rather than always using today.

## How to use the BISCS Age Calculator

1. Open the [Age Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/).
2. Select your **date of birth** in the first date field.
3. Leave **Age on** as today, or change it to the cut-off date from your form or notice. The "Today" button resets it.
4. Read your age in years, months and days at the top of the results.
5. Scroll down for totals in months, weeks, days, hours and minutes, and for your next birthday with a countdown.

The results also show the weekday you were born on, which is a nice detail for birthday cards or simply satisfying curiosity. The dates never leave your device.

## How exact age is calculated, step by step

Here is the method the tool follows, using a birth date of 15 August 1995 and a target date of 2 November 2026.

1. **Completed years.** The last birthday before the target date is 15 August 2026. From 1995 to 2026 is 31 completed years.
2. **Completed months.** From 15 August 2026, add months while you stay on or before 2 November: 15 September, 15 October. That is 2 months. Adding one more would reach 15 November, which is too far.
3. **Remaining days.** From 15 October to 2 November is 18 days (16 days left in October, plus 2 in November).
4. **Result.** 31 years, 2 months, 18 days.

For the totals, the tool counts every calendar day between the dates: 11,402 days in this example, which is 1,628 weeks and 6 days. The next birthday, 15 August 2027, is 286 days away.

### The month-end problem

What if you were born on 31 January? There is no 31 February, so when counting months the calculator uses the last day of shorter months instead. This keeps the result sensible and matches how most people think about month-end birthdays.

### Leap-day birthdays

If you were born on 29 February, your birthday only exists in leap years. In other years, the tool counts 28 February as your birthday and shows a note to explain this. Some institutions may use 1 March instead, so for legal documents follow the rule of the body that asked.

## Common mistakes when calculating age

- **Subtracting only the years.** 2026 − 1995 = 31, but if the birthday has not arrived yet this year, the person is still 30.
- **Using today instead of the cut-off date.** For exam eligibility, the date in the notice is what counts.
- **Assuming every month has 30 days.** This can throw off the day count by one or two days, which matters near age limits.
- **Ignoring leap years** when converting age to days. A flat 365 per year undercounts.
- **Entering the date in the wrong format.** If you type a date manually elsewhere, 05/08 can mean 5 August or 8 May. The date picker avoids this confusion.

## Quick checklist before submitting a form

- Does the date of birth match your official document, such as the Class 10 certificate, birth certificate or passport?
- Is the "Age on" date exactly the one stated in the notice?
- Have you noted the result as years, months and days if the form asks for all three?
- If you are close to a limit, have you checked any age relaxation for your category?

## Other ways people use an age calculator

Beyond forms, an age calculator is handy for:

- **Milestones.** Find when you will be 10,000 days old, or how many weeks a baby has been born.
- **Family records.** Work out grandparents' ages for insurance renewals or pension paperwork.
- **Pets and vehicles.** The same maths gives the age of a car from its registration date, or a dog from its adoption day.
- **Event planning.** Check which year someone turns 50 or 60 and plan a celebration ahead.

If you need the gap between any two dates, not just a birthday, the [Date Difference calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/date-difference-calculator/) also gives working days and weeks. To find a date a set number of days ahead, such as a 90-day deadline, use [Add or Subtract Days](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/date-add-calculator/). For retirement planning, the [Gratuity Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/gratuity-calculator/) uses years of service in a similar way.

## Is an online age calculator accurate?

A good one is exact, because it counts real calendar dates rather than approximating. The BISCS tool works in whole days using the calendar, so time zones and daylight saving cannot shift the answer. It does not consider the time of birth, so on your birthday itself the result shows exactly the new age from the start of the day.

For legal or official purposes, the age shown on your documents and the organisation's own rules always take priority. Use the calculator to check and plan, then confirm against the official notice. When you are ready, open the [Age Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/) and get your answer in a couple of taps.

Q: How do I calculate age as on a specific date for a government exam?
A: Enter your date of birth and set the “Age on” field to the cut-off date given in the recruitment notice, not today’s date. The result in years, months and days is what you compare with the minimum and maximum age limits. Always read the notice for relaxation rules for reserved categories.

Q: How is age counted for someone born on 29 February?
A: In non-leap years, the BISCS Age Calculator treats 28 February as the birthday, which is the convention most people follow. Legal treatment can differ between countries and institutions, so for official purposes check the rule used by the organisation asking for your age.

Q: Why does my age in days not match years multiplied by 365?
A: Because of leap years. Every four years or so an extra day is added, so a 31-year span contains about seven or eight leap days. The calculator counts actual calendar days between the two dates, so its total is exact.

Q: Does the calculator store my date of birth?
A: No. The calculation runs entirely in your browser, and the dates you enter are not uploaded or saved on a server. Closing the page clears them, so you can safely use it for family members’ details too.

## Base64 Encode and Decode Online: What It Is and When to Use It

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/base64-encode-decode-explained/
Tool: Base64 Encode / Decode (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/base64-encoder/)

Quick answer: Base64 converts any data, including images or Unicode text, into a string of 64 safe ASCII characters so it can travel through systems built for text. It is encoding, not encryption: anyone can decode it. BISCS India's Base64 tool encodes and decodes text or files, with URL-safe mode, entirely in your browser.

Base64 is a way of writing any data, whether text, an image or a PDF, using only 64 plain characters: `A–Z`, `a–z`, `0–9`, `+` and `/`. It exists because many systems, from email to JSON to HTML, were built to carry text and can corrupt raw binary bytes.

The most important thing to know is that Base64 is **encoding, not encryption**. It hides nothing. The [Base64 Encode / Decode](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/base64-encoder/) tool on BISCS India converts both ways in your browser, handles Hindi, Bengali and emoji correctly, and can turn whole files into Base64 strings.

## How does Base64 work?

Computers store data as bytes of 8 bits. Base64 takes 3 bytes (24 bits) at a time, splits them into four 6-bit groups, and maps each group to one of 64 characters. When the input length is not a multiple of 3, the output is padded with one or two `=` signs.

The word `Hi!` is three bytes, so it becomes exactly four characters:

```text
Hi!      ->  SGkh
Hello    ->  SGVsbG8=
```

Because 3 bytes become 4 characters, Base64 output is always about one third larger than the input.

## Where you will meet Base64

- **Data URLs.** Small images embedded directly in CSS or HTML, such as `data:image/png;base64,iVBORw0…`.
- **Email attachments.** MIME email encodes attachments in Base64, wrapped at 76 characters per line.
- **JSON Web Tokens.** The header and payload of a JWT are base64url-encoded JSON.
- **HTTP Basic authentication.** The `Authorization: Basic …` header carries `username:password` in Base64, which is exactly why it must only be sent over HTTPS.
- **APIs that accept files.** Some government and business APIs, including several used for e-invoicing and document upload, expect file contents as a Base64 string inside JSON.

## Encoding is not encryption

This is the mistake that causes real security incidents. A developer stores an API key or password as Base64 in a config file or front-end code, thinking it is "encrypted". It is not. Decoding it is one click:

```js
atob('cGFzc3dvcmQxMjM=');  // "password123"
```

Use Base64 to make data **transportable**, never to make it **secret**. For secrecy you need encryption with a key; for storing passwords you need a slow password hash such as bcrypt or Argon2.

## How to encode or decode with BISCS India

1. Open [Base64 Encode / Decode](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/base64-encoder/).
2. Choose **Encode** or **Decode** at the top.
3. Type or paste your text into the left box. The result appears instantly on the right, with the byte size of each side.
4. Optional: tick **URL-safe (- _ no padding)** for base64url output, or **Wrap lines at 76 chars** for email-style formatting.
5. Use **Swap** to send the output back to the input and flip the mode, which is a quick way to check a round trip.
6. Click **Copy**, or **Download** to save the result. When decoding binary data, Download saves the original bytes.

### Encoding a file

Scroll to **File to Base64**, choose a file (up to 25 MB) and the Base64 appears in the output box. Keep **Include data: URL prefix** ticked if you want a ready-to-use `data:` URL, or untick it for the bare Base64 string that most APIs expect. For images specifically, the [Image to Base64](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-to-base64/) tool adds previews and ready-made HTML and CSS snippets.

## Unicode: why the Sample uses ₹ and नमस्ते

The browser’s built-in `btoa()` function throws an error on any character outside Latin-1, which rules out Hindi, Tamil, the rupee sign and emoji. The correct approach is to convert the text to UTF-8 bytes first:

```js
const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode('₹ नमस्ते');
const b64 = btoa(String.fromCharCode(...bytes));
```

The tool does this for you. When decoding, it checks that the bytes are valid UTF-8. If they are not, it shows a warning that the data is binary and offers a download instead of printing gibberish.

## Standard vs URL-safe Base64

| | Standard | URL-safe (base64url) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Characters 62 and 63 | `+` and `/` | `-` and `_` |
| Padding | `=` at the end | Usually omitted |
| Used in | Email, data URLs, most APIs | JWTs, URL parameters, file names |

The decoder accepts either variant, ignores whitespace and line breaks, and strips a leading `data:…;base64,` prefix automatically.

## Common mistakes with Base64

- **Treating it as security.** Covered above, but worth repeating.
- **Embedding big images as data URLs.** The 33% size increase and loss of browser caching usually make pages slower. Inline only tiny icons.
- **Double encoding.** Encoding an already-encoded string produces valid but useless output. If a decoded result still looks like Base64, it was encoded twice.
- **Mixing up Base64 and URL encoding.** A `+` in standard Base64 inside a URL may be read as a space. Use URL-safe Base64, or percent-encode the string with the [URL Encode / Decode](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/url-encoder/) tool.
- **Breaking padding.** Removing or adding `=` characters by hand can make strict decoders reject the string.

## Privacy

Encoding happens in your browser with JavaScript. Text you type and files you select are never uploaded. That matters, because the strings people decode are often tokens and credentials. If you are inspecting a JWT, the [JWT Decoder](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/jwt-decoder/) splits it into header and payload for you, again without sending it anywhere.

Q: Is Base64 a form of encryption?
A: No. Base64 is a reversible encoding with no key or secret. Anyone who sees a Base64 string can decode it in seconds. Never use it to hide passwords, API keys or personal data. If you need secrecy, use real encryption such as AES, and transport data over HTTPS.

Q: Why is Base64 output bigger than the original?
A: Base64 represents every 3 bytes of input as 4 characters, so output is about 33% larger, plus up to two = padding characters. A 300 KB image becomes roughly 400 KB of Base64 text. That overhead is why embedding large images as Base64 in web pages is usually a bad idea.

Q: What is URL-safe Base64?
A: Standard Base64 uses + and /, which have special meanings in URLs. URL-safe Base64, also called base64url, replaces them with - and _ and usually drops the = padding. JSON Web Tokens use this variant. The BISCS India decoder accepts both forms automatically.

Q: Why does decoding give me garbled text?
A: The original data was probably binary, such as an image, PDF or compressed file, rather than text. The tool detects this and warns you. Use Download to save the decoded bytes as a file, then rename it with the correct extension if you know what it is.

Q: Why does btoa() fail on Hindi or emoji text?
A: The browser function btoa only accepts characters in the Latin-1 range. To encode Unicode text you must first convert it to UTF-8 bytes, for example with TextEncoder, and then Base64-encode those bytes. The BISCS India tool does this automatically, so any language works.

## BMI Calculator Guide: Formula, Categories and Indian Cut-offs

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/bmi-calculator-indian-cut-offs-explained/
Tool: BMI Calculator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/bmi-calculator/)

Quick answer: BMI (Body Mass Index) is your weight in kilograms divided by your height in metres squared. Under WHO categories, 18.5–24.9 is a healthy range, but guidelines commonly used in India treat 23 and above as overweight for Asian Indian adults. BMI is a screening estimate only; BISCS India’s BMI Calculator shows both scales.

Body Mass Index (BMI) is your weight in kilograms divided by the square of your height in metres. A person who is 170 cm tall and weighs 68 kg has a BMI of 68 ÷ (1.70 × 1.70) = 23.5.

Whether 23.5 counts as "healthy" depends on which scale you use. Under the general WHO categories it is in the healthy range, but under the lower cut-offs commonly used for Asian Indian adults it falls just into "overweight". The free [BMI Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/bmi-calculator/) shows you either scale with one tick box.

**Important:** BMI is a quick screening estimate, not a diagnosis. It does not measure body fat directly, and it should not replace advice from a doctor or registered dietitian.

## What is the BMI formula?

The formula is the same everywhere:

**BMI = weight (kg) ÷ height (m)²**

If you measure in feet and pounds, convert first, or let the calculator do it. For example, 5 feet 7 inches is 67 inches, or 1.70 m, and 150 lb is about 68.0 kg. That gives a BMI of about 23.5, the same as the metric example above.

## BMI categories: WHO and Asian Indian cut-offs

Research has found that people of South Asian origin tend to have more body fat, especially around the waist, and a higher risk of type 2 diabetes and heart disease at a lower BMI than many other populations. For this reason, guidelines commonly cited in India use lower thresholds for adults.

| Category | WHO (general) | Asian / Indian cut-offs (commonly cited) |
|---|---|---|
| Underweight | Below 18.5 | Below 18.5 |
| Healthy weight | 18.5 – 24.9 | 18.5 – 22.9 |
| Overweight | 25 – 29.9 | 23 – 24.9 |
| Obese | 30 and above | 25 and above |

Different sources word these slightly differently. Some Indian guidance, for example, puts the lower end of normal at 18.0 rather than 18.5. The broad message is the same: for Indian adults, a BMI from 23 upwards deserves attention earlier than the WHO scale would suggest. Your doctor may also use other measures before drawing conclusions.

## How to check your BMI with the BISCS tool

1. Open the [BMI Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/bmi-calculator/).
2. Choose **Metric (cm, kg)** or **Imperial (ft, lb)**. Values carry over if you switch.
3. Enter your height and weight. Use a recent weight taken in light clothing.
4. Tick **Use Asian / Indian cut-offs** if you want the lower thresholds.
5. Read your BMI, category and position on the coloured scale.
6. Check the **healthy weight range** for your height, and the approximate change needed to reach it.

The tool also shows **BMI Prime**, which is your BMI divided by the upper limit of the healthy range for the scale you chose. A value below 1.0 means you are under that upper limit. Nothing you enter is uploaded, because the maths runs on your device.

## Worked example: the same person on two scales

Take Rahul, 170 cm and 68 kg, BMI 23.5.

- **WHO scale:** healthy. His healthy weight range is about 53.5 kg to 72.0 kg.
- **Asian cut-offs:** overweight, just above the 22.9 limit. His healthy range becomes about 53.5 kg to 66.2 kg, so the tool suggests losing about 1.8 kg to reach it.

Now take Priya, 160 cm and 82 kg. Her BMI is 82 ÷ 2.56 = 32.0, which is obese on both scales. The calculator shows a target that brings her into the healthy range, but a safe plan and pace should come from a doctor or dietitian, not from a number alone.

## What BMI cannot tell you

BMI is popular because it needs only a tape and a scale. Its limits are just as important:

- **It ignores body composition.** Muscle weighs more than fat for the same volume, so sportspeople and gym regulars can read as "overweight" while being fit.
- **It does not show where fat sits.** Fat around the abdomen carries more health risk than fat elsewhere.
- **It is for adults only.** Children and teenagers need age- and sex-specific growth charts.
- **It is not meant for pregnancy.** Weight gain during pregnancy follows different guidance.
- **It can miss risk in older adults,** who may lose muscle while keeping the same weight.

### Add a waist measurement

Many clinicians pair BMI with waist circumference. Thresholds commonly cited for Indian adults are around 90 cm for men and 80 cm for women, above which abdominal obesity is considered more likely. Measure midway between your lowest rib and the top of your hip bone, breathing out normally.

## Common mistakes when checking BMI

- Using height in centimetres without converting to metres (68 ÷ 170² gives a meaningless 0.0024).
- Weighing after a heavy meal or in shoes and outdoor clothes.
- Relying on an old height measurement. Adults can lose a little height with age.
- Reading a single result as a diagnosis rather than a reason to check further.
- Comparing your number with a friend's who uses a different scale.

## What to do with your result

If your BMI is in the healthy range, keep up regular activity and a balanced diet, and recheck every few months. If it is below or above the range:

- **Talk to a doctor** for a basic check-up. Blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol tests give far more insight than BMI alone.
- **See a registered dietitian** for a plan that fits your food habits, budget and any medical conditions.
- **Aim for gradual change.** Sudden crash diets are hard to sustain and can be unsafe.

To understand how much energy your body uses each day, try the [Calorie Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/calorie-calculator/), which estimates your BMR and maintenance calories. If your scale or tape uses unfamiliar units, the [Unit Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/unit-converter/) converts pounds, stones, feet and inches. And for an exact age to go with a health form, use the [Age Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/age-calculator/).

BMI is a useful first look, not the full story. Use the [BMI Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/bmi-calculator/) to know where you stand, then let a qualified professional help you decide what, if anything, to change.

Q: What is a healthy BMI for Indians?
A: Guidelines commonly cited in India suggest a BMI of roughly 18.5 to 22.9 as the healthy range for Asian Indian adults, with 23 to 24.9 classed as overweight and 25 or above as obese. These lower cut-offs reflect higher health risks at lower BMI seen in South Asian populations. A doctor can interpret your figure in context.

Q: Is BMI accurate for athletes and older adults?
A: Not always. BMI cannot tell muscle from fat, so muscular people can show a high BMI while being healthy, and older adults may have a normal BMI with low muscle and more body fat. Waist measurement, body composition and a medical check-up give a fuller picture.

Q: Can I use this BMI calculator for my child?
A: No. Adult BMI categories are meant for people aged 18 and over. Children and teenagers are assessed with BMI-for-age growth charts that compare them with others of the same age and sex. Ask a paediatrician to plot your child’s height and weight correctly.

Q: What should I do if my BMI is outside the healthy range?
A: Treat it as a prompt for a conversation, not a diagnosis. Book a check-up with a doctor, who may measure waist size, blood pressure, blood sugar and cholesterol. A registered dietitian can then suggest realistic changes to food and activity that suit your health and routine.

Q: Does the BMI calculator save my weight or height?
A: No. Everything is calculated in your browser as you type, and your measurements are not sent to or stored on any server. You can check figures for family members privately.

## How Many Calories Do I Need a Day? BMR and TDEE Explained

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/how-many-calories-do-i-need-bmr-tdee/
Tool: Calorie Calculator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/calorie-calculator/)

Quick answer: Your daily calorie need is roughly your BMR (energy used at rest) multiplied by an activity factor, giving your TDEE or maintenance calories. BISCS India’s Calorie Calculator uses the Mifflin–St Jeor equation to estimate both, plus targets for gradual weight loss or gain. Treat the result as an estimate and consult a doctor or dietitian.

The number of calories you need each day depends on your body size, age, sex and how active you are. A common way to estimate it is to work out your **BMR** (the energy your body uses at rest) and multiply it by an **activity factor** to get your **TDEE** (total daily energy expenditure). Eating close to your TDEE keeps your weight roughly stable.

For a 30-year-old man who is 170 cm tall, weighs 70 kg and exercises lightly, that comes to about 2,224 kcal a day. The free [Calorie Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/calorie-calculator/) works this out for you in seconds.

**Please note:** these are estimates for healthy adults. They are not medical advice. If you have a health condition, are pregnant, or plan a significant change in diet, consult a doctor or registered dietitian.

## What are BMR and TDEE?

- **BMR (basal metabolic rate)** is the energy needed to keep you alive at complete rest: breathing, heartbeat, temperature and organ function. For most people it makes up the largest share of daily energy use.
- **TDEE (total daily energy expenditure)** is BMR plus everything else: walking, working, household chores, exercise and digesting food.

Your TDEE is your **maintenance calories**. Eat less than this on average and you tend to lose weight; eat more and you tend to gain.

## The formula behind the calculator

The BISCS tool uses the **Mifflin–St Jeor equation**, which is widely used by dietitians as a starting estimate:

- **Men:** BMR = 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age + 5
- **Women:** BMR = 10 × weight (kg) + 6.25 × height (cm) − 5 × age − 161

BMR is then multiplied by an activity factor:

| Activity level | Description | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|
| Sedentary | Little or no exercise | 1.2 |
| Light | Exercise 1–3 days a week | 1.375 |
| Moderate | Exercise 3–5 days a week | 1.55 |
| Active | Hard exercise 6–7 days a week | 1.725 |
| Very active | Physical job or training twice a day | 1.9 |

## How to use the BISCS Calorie Calculator

1. Open the [Calorie Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/calorie-calculator/).
2. Choose your **sex** and **units** (metric or imperial).
3. Enter your **age** (15 to 100), **height** and **weight**.
4. Pick the **activity level** that matches a typical week.
5. Read your maintenance calories at the top, with your BMR shown beside it.
6. Check the **goal table** for calorie targets to lose, maintain or gain weight, and the suggested macro split.

The calculation happens in your browser, so your age and weight are not uploaded anywhere.

## Worked examples

### Arjun: light activity, wants to lose weight slowly

Arjun is 30, 170 cm and 70 kg, and goes to the gym twice a week.

- BMR = 700 + 1,062.5 − 150 + 5 = 1,617.5, shown as about 1,618 kcal.
- TDEE = 1,617.5 × 1.375 ≈ 2,224 kcal.
- A 500 kcal daily deficit gives a target of about 1,724 kcal.

At maintenance, the suggested split of 25% protein, 50% carbohydrate and 25% fat works out to about 139 g protein, 278 g carbohydrate and 62 g fat. These are starting points; a dietitian may adjust them for his goals.

### Meena: sedentary desk job

Meena is 28, 158 cm and 60 kg, and rarely exercises.

- BMR = 600 + 987.5 − 140 − 161 = 1,286.5, about 1,287 kcal.
- TDEE = 1,286.5 × 1.2 ≈ 1,544 kcal.
- A 500 kcal deficit would mean about 1,044 kcal a day.

The calculator marks that last figure as **low**, because it is below roughly 1,200 kcal. For Meena, a milder 250 kcal deficit (about 1,294 kcal) combined with more daily movement is a more sustainable option, and worth discussing with a professional.

## How fast can you safely lose or gain weight?

The goal table uses rough rules of thumb: a deficit of about 500 kcal a day is often linked to around 0.5 kg of loss per week, and 250 kcal to around 0.25 kg. Real results vary because water, muscle, hormones and how accurately you track food all play a part.

Gradual change is usually easier to sustain. Very low intakes can make it hard to get enough protein and micronutrients, and the tool deliberately flags targets below about 1,200 kcal for women and 1,500 kcal for men. Going under those levels should only happen with medical supervision.

## Common mistakes with calorie targets

- **Overstating activity.** Choosing "Active" because of one intense week inflates the number.
- **Treating the result as exact.** Formulas estimate averages; your real need may be a few hundred calories different.
- **Forgetting cooking oil, ghee and drinks.** Tea with sugar, juices and the oil in a tadka add up quickly.
- **Changing everything at once.** Adjust intake by small steps and watch the trend for two to four weeks.
- **Ignoring protein.** A low-calorie diet that is also low in protein can cost muscle.
- **Using it for children, teenagers or pregnancy.** These need professional guidance.

## Practical tips

- Weigh yourself at the same time of day, a few times a week, and look at the weekly average.
- Read nutrition labels on packaged foods; they list energy per serving and per 100 g.
- Recalculate after a change of 3 to 5 kg, since your needs change with your weight.
- Combine diet changes with activity. Even a daily brisk walk raises your TDEE.

For a quick health snapshot alongside this, the [BMI Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/bmi-calculator/) shows your BMI on both WHO and Asian Indian scales. If your recipes use cups, ounces or pounds, the [Unit Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/unit-converter/) handles kitchen units. And to time workouts or intervals, try the [Stopwatch & Timer](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/stopwatch-timer/).

Calorie numbers are a helpful guide, not a rulebook. Use the [Calorie Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/calorie-calculator/) to get a sensible starting point, then let your progress, and a qualified dietitian or doctor, shape the details.

Q: What is the difference between BMR and TDEE?
A: BMR, or basal metabolic rate, is the energy your body uses at complete rest to keep you alive: breathing, circulation and organ function. TDEE, or total daily energy expenditure, adds the energy used in daily movement and exercise. TDEE is the figure to use as your maintenance calories.

Q: How accurate is a calorie calculator?
A: It gives a reasonable starting estimate, not an exact measurement. Formulas such as Mifflin–St Jeor are based on population averages, so an individual’s real needs can differ noticeably. Track your weight for a few weeks at a given intake and adjust gradually, ideally with guidance from a dietitian.

Q: Is it safe to eat 1,000 calories a day to lose weight fast?
A: Very low intakes are generally not advisable without medical supervision. They can make it hard to get enough protein, vitamins and minerals, and are difficult to sustain. The calculator flags targets below about 1,200 kcal for women and 1,500 kcal for men. Speak to a doctor before trying any aggressive diet.

Q: Which activity level should I choose?
A: Pick the level that matches your typical week, not your best week. Most people with desk jobs and a few workouts fit “Light” or “Moderate”. If you are unsure, choose the lower option, then adjust after watching your weight trend for two to four weeks.

Q: Can I use this calculator during pregnancy or for a child?
A: No. The formula is designed for healthy adults and does not account for pregnancy, breastfeeding, growth in children and teenagers, or medical conditions that affect metabolism. In those situations, calorie needs should come from a doctor or registered dietitian.

## Case Converter: Change Text to UPPER, lower or Title Case

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/convert-text-case-upper-lower-title/
Tool: Case Converter (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/case-converter/)

Quick answer: To change the case of text, paste it into a case converter and click the style you want, such as UPPER CASE, lower case, Title Case or Sentence case. BISCS India’s Case Converter also handles camelCase, snake_case and kebab-case line by line, with undo, and runs entirely in your browser.

A case converter changes the capitalisation of text without retyping it. Paste a paragraph typed with caps lock on, click **lower case** or **Sentence case**, and it is fixed in one go. The same tool can turn a heading into Title Case or a list of field names into `snake_case` for code.

It is one of those small tools that saves real time, especially when text arrives from forms, spreadsheets or old documents where nobody cared about consistent capitals.

## Which text cases can you convert to?

The BISCS India [Case Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/case-converter/) offers twelve styles, split into everyday writing and programming formats.

| Style | Example | Typical use |
|---|---|---|
| UPPER CASE | PAY BEFORE 20 JULY | Notices, short labels, form fields that demand capitals |
| lower case | pay before 20 july | Cleaning up shouty text before editing |
| Title Case | How to Apply for a PAN Card | Blog titles, book and report headings |
| Sentence case | How to apply for a PAN card | Body text, news-style headlines, buttons |
| aLtErNaTiNg | pAy BeFoRe | Memes and playful social posts |
| iNVERSE cASE | pAY bEFORE | Fixing text typed with caps lock accidentally on |
| camelCase | invoiceTotalAmount | JavaScript and Java variables |
| PascalCase | InvoiceTotalAmount | Class and component names |
| snake_case | invoice_total_amount | Python, database columns |
| kebab-case | invoice-total-amount | URLs, CSS classes, file names |
| CONSTANT_CASE | INVOICE_TOTAL_AMOUNT | Environment variables, constants |
| dot.case | invoice.total.amount | Config keys, some translation files |

Notice that the PAN acronym in the examples above would not survive a blanket lower-case conversion. More on that below.

## How to change text case online

1. Open the [Case Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/case-converter/).
2. Paste or type your text into the box. The word and character count appears above it.
3. Click the style you want from the grid of buttons. The text is converted in place.
4. Not quite right? Press **Undo** to go back, then try another style.
5. Press **Copy** to put the result on your clipboard, or **Download** to save it as a `.txt` file.

Everything runs inside your browser tab, so customer names, addresses or internal notes you paste are not uploaded anywhere.

## Title Case vs Sentence case: which should you use?

Both are correct, and style guides disagree, so the main rule is to pick one and be consistent.

**Title Case** gives headings a formal, traditional look. The BISCS converter follows the common convention of leaving short words such as "a", "an", "the", "and", "of", "in", "to" and "with" in lower case, unless they are the first or last word or come straight after a colon. So "a guide to gst for small shops" becomes "A Guide to Gst for Small Shops".

**Sentence case** reads more naturally and is easier to scan, which is why many government portals, apps and news sites use it for headings and buttons. The converter capitalises the first letter after each full stop, question mark, exclamation mark or Hindi purna viram, and fixes a lone "i" to "I".

Look at that Title Case example again: "Gst" is wrong. That leads to the most important tip.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Losing acronyms and proper nouns.** No converter can tell that GST, PAN, UPI, Kolkata or your company name should stay as they are. Always proofread after converting and fix them by hand.
- **Using UPPER CASE for long text.** Paragraphs in capitals are harder to read and come across as shouting in emails and WhatsApp messages. Keep capitals for short labels.
- **Converting code that is already mixed.** The programming styles split words at spaces, punctuation and changes from lower to upper case, so `HTTPServerError` becomes `http_server_error`. Check edge cases like version numbers.
- **Expecting Indian scripts to change.** Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and most Indian scripts have no capital letters, so they are left untouched.

## Tips for developers and data work

The programming styles treat each line separately. That makes the tool handy for bulk renaming:

- Paste the header row of a spreadsheet, one column name per line, and convert to `snake_case` before importing into a database.
- Turn a list of labels like "First Name", "Date of Birth" and "PAN Number" into `camelCase` JSON keys: `firstName`, `dateOfBirth`, `panNumber`.
- Convert component names to `kebab-case` for file names and CSS classes.

If you are building URLs from page titles, the dedicated [Slug Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/slug-generator/) is a better fit because it also strips punctuation, handles accents and can drop stop words. When you need to rename one term throughout a long file rather than change case, use [Find and Replace](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/find-and-replace/).

## Fixing text copied from forms and spreadsheets

Data entered by many different people is rarely consistent. A customer list may contain "RAMESH KUMAR", "priya sharma" and "Anil  verma" in the same column. A quick clean-up routine looks like this:

1. Paste the column into the Case Converter and choose **Title Case** for names.
2. Copy the result into the [Whitespace Cleaner](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/whitespace-cleaner/) to remove the double spaces.
3. Check initials and surnames such as "D'Souza" or "McDonald", which may need a manual fix.

For addresses, keep in mind that PIN codes and state abbreviations like "WB" or "MH" need to stay in capitals.

## Does the case converter save my text?

No. The conversion happens with JavaScript in your browser, so nothing is sent to BISCS India's servers. The undo history lasts only while the page is open, up to 50 steps, and disappears when you close the tab or clear the box.

That makes it suitable for working on client lists, unpublished articles or internal documents, though as always it is wise to use your own device for anything sensitive.

Q: What is the difference between Title Case and Sentence case?
A: Title Case capitalises the main words of a heading, as in How to File Your Income Tax Return, while leaving short words like of, and, to in lower case. Sentence case capitalises only the first word and proper nouns, as in How to file your income tax return. News sites and government pages increasingly prefer sentence case.

Q: Will the converter keep names like Delhi or GST in capitals?
A: Not automatically. A tool cannot know which words are proper nouns or acronyms, so Sentence case and lower case will turn GST into gst and Delhi into delhi. After converting, scan the result and fix names, brands and abbreviations by hand. The undo button lets you step back if needed.

Q: Can I convert a list of variable names at once?
A: Yes. The programming styles, camelCase, PascalCase, snake_case, kebab-case, CONSTANT_CASE and dot.case, work line by line. Paste one name per line, click a style, and every line is converted separately, which is handy for database columns, JSON keys or CSS class names.

Q: Does it work with Hindi or other scripts?
A: Scripts such as Devanagari, Bengali and Tamil do not have upper and lower case, so those letters stay as they are. Any English words mixed into the text are converted normally. Accented Latin letters, such as those in French or German names, are handled correctly.

Q: How do I undo a conversion?
A: Click Undo above the text box. The tool remembers up to 50 previous versions of your text in the current session, so you can try several styles and step back through them. Clearing the page or closing the tab removes that history.

## How to Convert CSV to JSON Online (Quotes, Types, Headers)

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/convert-csv-to-json-online/
Tool: CSV to JSON (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/)

Quick answer: To convert CSV to JSON, paste the CSV into a converter that reads the first row as headers and turns each following row into a JSON object. BISCS India's CSV to JSON tool auto-detects the delimiter, handles quoted commas and line breaks, optionally converts numbers and booleans, and runs fully in your browser.

Converting CSV to JSON means reading a table and writing each row out as an object whose keys come from the header row. A two-line CSV like `name,city` / `Asha,Delhi` becomes `[{"name": "Asha", "city": "Delhi"}]`.

That sounds simple, until you meet a value with a comma in it, a note that spans two lines, or a semicolon-separated file from a European tool. The [CSV to JSON](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/) converter on BISCS India follows the CSV standard (RFC 4180) closely, so those cases come out right, and it all happens in your browser.

## Why convert CSV to JSON?

Spreadsheets are where data is born in most offices. JSON is what applications want. You might need to:

- Seed a database or a test fixture from a list someone maintained in Excel.
- Feed a product catalogue or price list into a website or app.
- Send records to an API that accepts JSON only.
- Load a lookup table, such as state codes or HSN categories, into JavaScript.

Writing that JSON by hand is slow and error-prone. A converter does it in a second.

## A worked example

Here is a small CSV with a few awkward values:

```text
id,name,city,amount,paid,notes
1,Asha Verma,Delhi,2500.50,true,
2,"Das, Rohan",Kolkata,1200,false,"Said ""call later"""
```

With the default settings, the output is:

```json
[
  { "id": 1, "name": "Asha Verma", "city": "Delhi", "amount": 2500.5, "paid": true, "notes": "" },
  { "id": 2, "name": "Das, Rohan", "city": "Kolkata", "amount": 1200, "paid": false, "notes": "Said \"call later\"" }
]
```

The quoted `"Das, Rohan"` stays a single value. The doubled quotes `""` turn into a literal quote, which JSON then escapes as `\"`. And because type detection is on, `2500.50` is a number and `true` is a boolean rather than strings.

## How to convert CSV to JSON with BISCS India

1. Open [CSV to JSON](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/).
2. Paste your CSV, drag a `.csv`, `.tsv` or `.txt` file onto the box, or click **Upload**.
3. Leave **Delimiter** on **Auto-detect** unless the result looks wrong. It checks comma, semicolon, tab and pipe and picks the one that gives the most consistent column count.
4. Choose the **Output**: **Array of objects** (most common) or **Array of arrays** (smaller, positional).
5. Set the options: **First row is header**, **Detect numbers, booleans & null**, **Empty cells as null**, **Skip empty lines** and **Minify**.
6. Check the table in **Preview** and the status line, which reports rows, columns, the delimiter used and any rows with missing cells.
7. Click **Copy** or **Download .json**.

## Array of objects or array of arrays?

| Output | Looks like | Use it when |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Array of objects | `[{"name":"Asha","city":"Delhi"}]` | Sending to APIs, databases, most code |
| Array of arrays | `[["name","city"],["Asha","Delhi"]]` | Charts, compact storage, column order matters |

Objects are self-describing and easier to work with in code. Arrays repeat no key names, so they are smaller for large tables.

## When should you turn off type detection?

Type detection is convenient, but some values only look like numbers. Switch it off, or check the output carefully, for:

- **Account numbers, Aadhaar-style IDs and long reference numbers.** The tool only converts numbers up to 15 significant digits, so longer IDs stay as strings. Shorter IDs still become numbers, which may not be what your system expects.
- **Codes with leading zeros.** `0042` is kept as a string, because `0042` is not a valid JSON number. Good, but be aware the column then has mixed types if other rows are plain numbers.
- **Version numbers and phone numbers.** `10.20` becomes the number `10.2`, losing the trailing zero.

If in doubt, keep everything as strings and convert the specific fields you need in your own code.

## Common mistakes and how to spot them

- **Unquoted commas.** `Mumbai, Maharashtra` without quotes splits into two cells. The status bar warns about rows with a different number of columns.
- **An unclosed quote.** One stray `"` can swallow the rest of the file into a single value. The converter flags "Unclosed quote at the end of the file" when this happens.
- **Duplicate or blank headers.** Two columns both called `phone` would overwrite each other in an object. The tool renames the second one `phone_2`, and blank headers become `column_1`, `column_2` and so on.
- **The wrong delimiter.** If everything lands in a single column, the file probably uses semicolons or tabs. Auto-detect usually catches this; otherwise choose manually.
- **Excel’s hidden encoding.** Save as "CSV UTF-8" in Excel so that Indian-language text and the ₹ sign survive. A byte order mark at the start of the file is removed automatically.

## Is my data uploaded anywhere?

No. The CSV is parsed by JavaScript running on the page, and the JSON is built in memory on your device. Text files up to 50 MB can be loaded, though very large files will take longer on a phone. Because nothing leaves your computer, you can safely convert staff lists, customer exports or price sheets.

## Related tools

To check or prettify the resulting JSON, open it in the [JSON Formatter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/), which also offers a collapsible tree view. Going the other direction, [JSON to CSV](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/) turns API data back into a spreadsheet-ready file. If your source is an `.xlsx` workbook rather than a CSV, start with the [Excel & CSV Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/excel-csv-converter/).

## A quick checklist before you use the JSON

- Row count in the status line matches what you expect.
- No warning about rows with missing cells or unclosed quotes.
- IDs and codes are strings if your system treats them as text.
- Empty cells are `""` or `null`, whichever your application expects.
- Key names are clean: no stray spaces, no duplicates.

Five seconds spent on this list saves a lot of head-scratching when the import fails later.

Q: How do I convert an Excel sheet to JSON?
A: Save or export the sheet as CSV first (File, Save As, CSV UTF-8 in Excel, or File, Download, CSV in Google Sheets). Then paste or upload the CSV into the converter. If you have an .xlsx file and no Excel, the BISCS India Excel and CSV Converter can produce the CSV for you.

Q: Why did my PIN code or phone number lose its leading zero?
A: With type detection on, a value like 0042 is kept as a string because numbers with leading zeros are not valid JSON numbers. However, the source CSV may already have lost the zero if Excel saved it as a number. Format such columns as Text in Excel before exporting.

Q: What does “Detect numbers, booleans & null” do?
A: CSV has no data types; every value is text. With this option on, values like 2500.50 become JSON numbers, true and false become booleans, and the word null becomes null. Turn it off when you need every value kept exactly as a string, for example IDs or codes.

Q: Can the converter handle commas inside a value?
A: Yes, as long as the value is wrapped in double quotes in the CSV, which is the standard. For example, "Das, Rohan" stays one value. Double quotes inside a quoted value are written as two quotes, and line breaks inside quotes are also preserved.

Q: What if some rows have fewer columns than the header?
A: The missing cells are filled with empty strings, or null if you tick Empty cells as null. The status line warns you how many rows were short, which often signals an unquoted comma or a broken line in the source file.

## EMI Calculator: Formula, Examples and Amortisation Explained

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/emi-calculator-formula-home-loan/
Tool: EMI Calculator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/emi-calculator/)

Quick answer: EMI is calculated as P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1), where P is the loan, r the monthly interest rate and n the number of months. A ₹25 lakh home loan at 8.5% for 20 years costs about ₹21,696 a month. BISCS India's free EMI Calculator also shows total interest and a yearly amortisation table.

An EMI (equated monthly instalment) is the fixed amount you pay every month to repay a loan with interest. It is calculated with the formula **EMI = P × r × (1 + r)^n ÷ ((1 + r)^n − 1)**, where P is the loan amount, r is the annual rate divided by 12 and by 100, and n is the tenure in months.

For example, a ₹25 lakh home loan at 8.5% a year for 20 years works out to about ₹21,696 a month. Over 240 months you repay roughly ₹52.07 lakh, so about ₹27.07 lakh of that is interest. The free [EMI Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/emi-calculator/) shows these numbers instantly and breaks them down year by year.

## How is EMI calculated, step by step?

Take the same ₹25 lakh loan:

1. **Monthly rate:** 8.5 ÷ 12 ÷ 100 = 0.0070833
2. **Months:** 20 × 12 = 240
3. **Growth factor:** (1.0070833)^240 ≈ 5.44
4. **EMI:** 25,00,000 × 0.0070833 × 5.44 ÷ (5.44 − 1) ≈ ₹21,696

You do not need to do this by hand, but seeing the steps helps you understand why the rate and tenure matter so much. The factor (1 + r)^n grows quickly with both, which is why small changes have a big effect over 20 years.

## How to use the BISCS EMI Calculator

1. Go to the [EMI Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/emi-calculator/).
2. Enter or slide the **loan amount** (the slider covers ₹50,000 to ₹2 crore; you can type other amounts).
3. Set the **interest rate** per year as quoted by your lender.
4. Choose whether to enter the tenure in **years** or **months**, then set it.
5. Read the monthly EMI, total interest and total payment, with a donut chart showing principal versus interest.
6. Scroll to the **amortisation schedule** for a chart of principal and interest paid each year, and open the table to see the closing balance and the percentage of the loan repaid.

The calculation runs entirely in your browser, so nothing about your loan is stored or uploaded.

## How do rate and tenure change your EMI?

Here is the same ₹25 lakh loan under three scenarios, calculated with the tool:

| Scenario | Monthly EMI | Total interest | Total paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8.5% for 20 years | ₹21,696 | ₹27.07 lakh | ₹52.07 lakh |
| 8.5% for 15 years | ₹24,618 | ₹19.31 lakh | ₹44.31 lakh |
| 9.0% for 20 years | ₹22,493 | ₹28.98 lakh | ₹53.98 lakh |

Two lessons stand out. Cutting five years off the tenure raises the EMI by about ₹2,900 but saves nearly ₹7.8 lakh of interest. And a half-percent higher rate adds about ₹800 to each EMI, which becomes almost ₹1.9 lakh over 20 years.

For a shorter loan, such as a ₹5 lakh personal loan at 10.5% for 5 years, the EMI is about ₹10,747 and total interest about ₹1.45 lakh.

## Reading the amortisation schedule

In the early years, most of each EMI pays interest. In month one of the home loan above, interest is about ₹17,708 and only about ₹3,987 reduces the principal. The balance falls slowly at first and then faster, because each month a little less interest is due.

This is why **prepayments early in the loan** have the biggest effect. Every rupee of principal you clear in year two stops attracting interest for the remaining 18 years. The schedule's "Loan paid" column shows how far along you are; on the ₹25 lakh example, only about 12% of the principal has been repaid after the first five years.

## When should you use an EMI calculator?

- **Before applying:** to check what loan size your monthly budget can carry. Many lenders look at how much of your income goes to EMIs, so a lower EMI can affect eligibility.
- **When comparing offers:** enter each lender's rate and tenure to compare total interest, not just the EMI.
- **After a rate change:** enter the outstanding balance, new rate and remaining months to see the new EMI.
- **When planning a prepayment:** reduce the loan amount by your prepayment and compare the outcomes of keeping the EMI or the tenure the same.

## Mistakes people make with loan EMIs

1. **Looking only at the EMI.** A lower EMI from a longer tenure usually means far more interest.
2. **Ignoring fees.** Processing fees, insurance bundled with the loan and GST on fees add to the real cost but are not part of the EMI formula.
3. **Assuming a floating rate stays fixed.** Model a rate rise of 1% or so to see if you could still manage.
4. **Forgetting the tax angle.** For a self-occupied home, interest on a home loan may be deductible up to ₹2 lakh a year under the old tax regime. Try the numbers in the [Income Tax Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/income-tax-calculator/) before assuming a benefit.
5. **Comparing flat-rate and reducing-balance quotes directly.** Some lenders quote a flat rate, which charges interest on the original amount throughout. The [Simple Interest](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/simple-interest-calculator/) tool shows how flat interest is worked out, and it is usually much costlier than the same reducing-balance rate.

## What the calculator does not cover

The tool assumes a fixed rate for the whole term and equal monthly instalments starting one month after disbursement. It does not model step-up EMIs, moratoriums, part-prepayments in the middle of the schedule or broken-period interest. For a full picture of how money grows or costs compound, the [Compound Interest](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/compound-interest-calculator/) calculator is a useful companion.

Treat these results as estimates for planning, not as a loan offer or financial advice. Your sanction letter and the lender's repayment schedule are the official figures, and RBI rules and your loan agreement govern rate resets and charges. If a decision is significant, discuss it with your bank or a qualified adviser.

Q: Does a longer tenure reduce the total cost of a loan?
A: No. A longer tenure lowers each EMI but increases total interest, because you borrow the money for longer. On ₹25 lakh at 8.5%, a 15-year term costs about ₹19.3 lakh in interest while a 20-year term costs about ₹27.1 lakh, even though the EMI drops by roughly ₹2,900.

Q: Why is most of my early EMI going towards interest?
A: Interest each month is charged on the outstanding balance, which is highest at the start. As the balance falls, the interest part shrinks and the principal part grows. In the first month of a ₹25 lakh, 8.5%, 20-year loan, about ₹17,708 of the ₹21,696 EMI is interest.

Q: Will my bank's EMI match this calculator exactly?
A: It should be very close for a fixed-rate loan, but small differences are normal. Banks may round the EMI, charge broken-period interest from the disbursement date, or use a slightly different day count. Processing fees, insurance and floating-rate resets are not included in a standard EMI formula.

Q: What happens to my EMI if the interest rate rises on a floating loan?
A: Lenders usually either increase the EMI or keep it the same and extend the tenure. Extending the tenure can add many months and a lot of interest. You can model a rate change by entering the outstanding balance, the new rate and the remaining months in the calculator.

Q: Is a zero-interest EMI really free?
A: Not always. Some no-cost EMI offers build the interest into the product price or pass on a discount you would otherwise have received, and processing fees or GST on interest may apply. Compare the total amount you will pay with the price for an outright purchase before deciding.

## How to Calculate GST: Add or Remove GST with CGST/SGST Split

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/gst-calculator-add-remove-gst/
Tool: GST Calculator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/)

Quick answer: To add GST, multiply the net price by the rate and add the result: ₹10,000 at 18% becomes ₹11,800. To remove GST from an inclusive price, divide by (1 + rate ÷ 100): ₹11,800 ÷ 1.18 = ₹10,000. BISCS India's free GST Calculator does both and shows the CGST/SGST or IGST split.

GST is calculated as a percentage of the taxable value of a sale. If a price excludes GST, multiply it by the rate and add that amount on top. If a price already includes GST, divide it by (1 + rate ÷ 100) to get the value before tax, then subtract to find the GST inside it.

For a sale within one state, the tax is split equally into CGST and SGST. For a sale from one state to another, the whole amount is charged as IGST. The free [GST Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/) on BISCS India does all of this as you type and shows the same amount at every common rate.

## What is the formula to add GST to a price?

When you quote a price "plus GST", the arithmetic is simple:

- **GST amount** = net price × rate ÷ 100
- **Total** = net price + GST amount

**Example:** A Pune-based designer bills a client in Pune ₹10,000 for a logo, at 18%.

- GST = 10,000 × 18 ÷ 100 = ₹1,800
- Total = ₹11,800
- Split: CGST 9% = ₹900, SGST 9% = ₹900

If the same client were in Bengaluru, the designer would charge IGST of ₹1,800 instead of the CGST/SGST pair. The total stays ₹11,800.

## How do you remove GST from an inclusive amount?

Retail prices, restaurant menus and many online listings already include GST. To find the taxable value, divide rather than subtract a percentage:

- **Net price** = inclusive total ÷ (1 + rate ÷ 100)
- **GST included** = inclusive total − net price

**Example:** A box of stationery costs ₹5,250 including 5% GST.

- Net price = 5,250 ÷ 1.05 = ₹5,000
- GST included = ₹250 (₹125 CGST + ₹125 SGST)

The most common error is taking 18% of the total and subtracting it. On ₹11,800 that gives 11,800 − 2,124 = ₹9,676, which is wrong by more than ₹300, because the 18% was originally calculated on ₹10,000, not on ₹11,800.

## How to use the BISCS GST Calculator

1. Open the [GST Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/).
2. Choose **Add GST (exclusive)** if your amount is before tax, or **Remove GST (inclusive)** if it already contains tax.
3. Type the amount in rupees. Commas are fine, and the field reformats when you leave it.
4. Pick a rate: 0.25%, 3%, 5%, 12%, 18%, 28% or 40%, or choose **Custom** and enter any rate up to 100%.
5. Select **Within state** for a CGST + SGST split or **Inter-state** for IGST.
6. Read the result card for the net amount, GST, the split and the total. Scroll down to the table to see the same amount worked out at every listed rate side by side.

Everything is calculated in your browser. The figures you enter are not sent anywhere, so you can check client invoices or supplier bills without sharing them.

## Which GST rate should you use?

The rate depends on the goods or services and is set by the GST Council through notifications. With effect from 22 September 2025, the structure was rationalised (often called "GST 2.0"): most goods and services now sit in the 5% and 18% slabs, and a 40% rate applies to certain luxury and sin goods. Special rates continue for a few categories, such as 3% on gold and jewellery and 0.25% on rough diamonds.

The calculator still offers 12% and 28% because older invoices, credit notes for earlier periods and some exceptions may need them. Treat the rate list as a convenience, not a ruling. Before you bill, look up your product's HSN or service's SAC code with the [HSN & SAC Code Finder](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/hsn-code-finder/) and confirm the current rate on the CBIC GST rate pages.

| Situation | Tax charged | Example on ₹10,000 at 18% |
|---|---|---|
| Seller and buyer in the same state | CGST + SGST, half each | ₹900 + ₹900 |
| Seller in a Union Territory without legislature, buyer in the same UT | CGST + UTGST | ₹900 + ₹900 |
| Seller and buyer in different states | IGST, full rate | ₹1,800 |
| Imports | IGST (plus customs duty) | ₹1,800 on the assessable value |

## When is a GST calculator most useful?

- **Quoting prices.** Freelancers and small businesses can check that "₹40,000 + GST" means ₹47,200 to the client at 18%.
- **Checking bills.** Restaurant, hotel and electronics bills sometimes mix inclusive and exclusive prices. Reverse calculation shows how much tax you actually paid.
- **Setting MRP.** If you want a shelf price of ₹999 inclusive of 5% GST, the taxable value is 999 ÷ 1.05 = ₹951.43, which helps you plan margins.
- **Reconciling purchases.** Before you claim input tax credit, a quick check of each supplier invoice can catch arithmetic slips.

## Common mistakes to avoid

1. **Subtracting the rate from an inclusive total.** Always divide by 1.18, 1.05 and so on.
2. **Charging CGST/SGST on an inter-state sale.** The place of supply decides the tax type. Charging the wrong one can mean paying the right tax again under the correct head and then claiming a refund of the wrong one.
3. **Splitting IGST.** IGST is never split; it is the full rate under one head.
4. **Using an outdated rate.** Rates for many items changed in September 2025. Copying a rate from an old invoice is risky.
5. **Ignoring rounding on high-volume billing.** Round each invoice consistently. Tiny paisa differences add up across thousands of bills.
6. **Applying GST before a trade discount.** If the discount is on the invoice, deduct it first. The [Discount Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/) can add GST after stacked discounts.

## Tips for small businesses and freelancers

Keep the calculator open in a tab while drafting quotes, and when you are ready to bill, move the figures into the free [Invoice Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/invoice-generator/). For B2B invoices, validate your customer's GST number first with the [GSTIN Validator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/gstin-validator/) so the tax lands in the right place in their records.

If you sell both within your state and outside it, keep a separate column for IGST in your sales register. It makes GSTR-1 preparation and the GSTR-3B summary much easier at month end.

## A note on accuracy

This calculator does the arithmetic correctly for any rate you enter, but it cannot tell you which rate or tax type legally applies to your supply. Classification, exemptions, reverse charge and place-of-supply rules can be subtle. This guide is general information, not tax advice. For anything beyond routine billing, check the GST portal and CBIC notifications, or ask a chartered accountant or GST practitioner who knows your business.

Q: How do I calculate GST backwards from the total amount?
A: Divide the GST-inclusive total by 1 plus the rate as a decimal. For 18% GST, divide by 1.18; for 5%, divide by 1.05. The answer is the taxable value, and the difference between the total and that value is the GST included in the price.

Q: Is CGST plus SGST the same as IGST?
A: In amount, yes. On an intra-state sale at 18%, you charge 9% CGST and 9% SGST, which together equal the 18% IGST you would charge on an inter-state sale. What differs is who receives the tax and how input tax credit is set off.

Q: Which GST rates are used after the September 2025 changes?
A: From 22 September 2025, GST rates were rationalised so that most goods and services fall in 5% or 18%, with 40% for certain luxury and sin goods. Special rates such as 3% for gold remain. Rates for specific items change by notification, so confirm the current rate on the CBIC website.

Q: Should GST be calculated on the discounted price or the MRP?
A: Generally GST is charged on the transaction value, so a discount shown on the invoice at the time of sale reduces the taxable value before GST is added. Post-sale discounts follow separate conditions. If you are unsure how a particular scheme is treated, check with a GST practitioner.

Q: Why does my bill show GST to the paisa but the calculator rounds?
A: The calculator shows amounts to two decimal places, which matches paisa-level billing. Businesses often round the final invoice total to the nearest rupee and show a small round-off line. That rounding is an accounting choice and does not change the tax rate applied.

## How to Compress an Image to a Target Size in KB (Free)

Tool: Compress Image (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/)

Quick answer: To compress an image to a specific size, open an image compressor, choose Target size, enter the limit in KB and download. BISCS India’s Compress Image tool finds the highest quality that fits, shrinks dimensions only if necessary, and works in your browser so your photos are never uploaded.

Compressing an image means making its file smaller, measured in KB or MB, while keeping it looking as close to the original as possible. You need it when a form rejects a photo for being too large, when an email bounces because of attachment size, or when a website loads slowly because of heavy pictures.

The [Compress Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/) tool from BISCS India handles JPG, PNG and WebP. You can either set a quality level yourself or type a target such as 50 KB and let the tool work out the best settings that fit.

## How does image compression actually work?

There are three ways to make an image file smaller, and good compressors combine them:

1. **Lower the encoding quality.** JPG and WebP throw away fine detail the eye barely notices. A quality of 75% often halves the file with no visible change.
2. **Reduce the dimensions.** A 4000 × 3000 photo has 12 million pixels. At 1600 × 1200 it has under 2 million, so even at the same quality the file is far smaller.
3. **Use a more efficient format.** A camera photo saved as PNG can be several times larger than the same photo as JPG. WebP is usually smaller still.

The target size mode in the BISCS India tool searches through quality levels to find the best one under your limit. Only if quality alone cannot get there does it start reducing the dimensions.

## Step by step: compress a photo to a target size

1. Open [Compress Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/) and add your photos. You can drop in several at once or paste an image with Ctrl + V.
2. Choose the mode at the top of the panel:
   - **Quality** if you just want smaller files and are happy to set the slider yourself.
   - **Target size** if a portal or app gives you a KB limit.
3. In Target size mode, type the limit in KB or tap a chip: 20 KB, 50 KB, 100 KB, 200 KB, 500 KB or 1 MB.
4. Optionally set a **Max width / height**, such as 1920 px for websites or 1280 px for email.
5. Pick the **Output format**. Auto keeps JPG for photos, uses WebP for images with transparency, and converts opaque PNGs to JPG.
6. Drag the comparison slider across the preview to check quality, read the before and after sizes, and download. Batches download as a ZIP.

## Quality settings and what to expect

| Quality setting | Typical use | What you will notice |
|---|---|---|
| 85–95% | Portfolios, printing, product hero shots | Practically identical to the original |
| 65–80% | Websites, WhatsApp, email, most forms | Hard to tell apart on screen; big savings |
| 40–60% | Very strict upload limits | Softer detail, some blockiness in plain areas |
| Below 40% | Last resort only | Visible artefacts, colour banding, smudged text |

## Compressing photos and signatures for Indian application forms

Recruitment and admission portals, such as those for SSC, UPSC, IBPS and other bank exams, state public service commissions and university admissions, almost always set a size range in KB for the photograph and the signature. Often there is both a minimum and a maximum, and sometimes fixed pixel dimensions as well.

These limits are not the same everywhere, and they change between notifications. Always read the current official notice or the portal’s upload instructions before you start, rather than relying on a number you saw on a forum.

A reliable workflow:

1. Crop the photo so the face is well framed, using [Crop Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-cropper/).
2. If dimensions are specified, set them exactly with [Resize Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-resizer/).
3. Compress with Target size set a little below the maximum, for example a few KB under it, to leave a safety margin.
4. Check that the result is above the minimum. If it is not, raise the target or the quality.
5. Make sure the format matches what the portal accepts, which is usually JPG.

The same approach works for scanned signatures, caste or income certificates saved as images, and thumb impressions.

## Practical tips

- **Start from the best original.** Compressing a photo that WhatsApp has already compressed piles new losses on old ones. Use the original camera file where possible.
- **Crop before you compress.** Removing empty wall or sky reduces the pixels the compressor has to fit into your limit, so the important part keeps more quality.
- **Screenshots are special.** Text-heavy screenshots look best as PNG or at high JPG quality. If they must be tiny, reduce the width rather than crushing the quality.
- **Watch the Saved figure.** If a file shows “Already optimised”, it was already efficient and further squeezing would only make it worse.
- **For PDFs, use a different tool.** If you need a smaller PDF rather than a smaller image, [Compress PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) is designed for that.

## Common mistakes

- **Aiming exactly at the limit.** Some portals count KB slightly differently. A file of exactly the maximum can still be rejected, so leave a small margin.
- **Compressing again and again.** Each pass at low quality adds more damage. If the result is too big, go back to the original and set a smaller target.
- **Ignoring the minimum size.** A 6 KB photo for a form that wants at least 20 KB will be refused just as firmly as an oversized one.
- **Choosing PNG for a photo and wondering why it will not shrink.** Switch to JPG or Auto.
- **Over-compressing a signature.** Thin pen strokes break up at low quality. Crop tightly and keep quality reasonable instead.

## Does it work offline and is it private?

The compression runs in your browser using its built-in image encoder. Your photos are not uploaded to any server, so personal pictures, ID scans and documents stay on your device. Large batches of high-resolution photos may take a little longer on an older phone, simply because the work is being done locally rather than on a remote machine.

Q: How do I reduce a photo to under 50 KB for a form?
A: Switch the compressor to Target size, type 50 or tap the 50 KB chip, and download. The tool tries different quality levels to find the best one that fits. If even the lowest sensible quality is too big, it reduces the pixel dimensions slightly as well.

Q: Why can’t the tool reach my target size?
A: Very small targets for very large or detailed images may be impossible without destroying the picture. The tool then gives you the smallest version it could make and tells you. Resizing to smaller dimensions first, or cropping away empty space, usually solves it.

Q: Will compression make my photo look blurry?
A: At moderate settings, around 60 to 80 percent quality, most photos look the same as the original on a phone or laptop screen. Problems appear at very low quality: blocky skies, smudged edges and colour banding. Use the before-and-after slider to judge for yourself.

Q: Why does my PNG barely get smaller?
A: PNG is lossless, so the quality slider has no effect on it. Large savings come from converting photos to JPG or WebP, or from reducing the maximum width. The Auto format option handles this by converting opaque PNG photos to JPG automatically.

Q: Is my photo too small if the form has a minimum size?
A: Some portals set a minimum as well as a maximum KB value. If your compressed file is below the minimum, raise the quality or choose a larger target size rather than enlarging the image. A higher quality JPG of the same dimensions will weigh more.

## Convert Images Between JPG, PNG and WebP Online for Free

Converting an image means saving the same picture in a different file format, such as turning a PNG screenshot into a JPG or a JPG photo into WebP. You do it because a website only accepts a certain format, because you need a smaller file, or because you want to keep a transparent background.

The free [Convert Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-converter/) tool from BISCS India converts between JPG, PNG and WebP directly in your browser. Add one file or a whole batch, pick a format, and download.

## JPG, PNG or WebP: which format should you use?

Each format was designed for a different job. Choosing the right one matters more than any quality slider.

| Format | Best for | Transparency | Typical file size | Watch out for |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JPG (JPEG) | Photos, form uploads, printing | No | Small | Text and sharp edges can blur slightly |
| PNG | Screenshots, logos, graphics, cut-outs | Yes | Large for photos | Big files when used for camera photos |
| WebP | Websites and apps | Yes | Smallest | A few older portals and programs still reject it |

A simple rule: photos go to JPG (or WebP for websites), anything with flat colours, text or a transparent background goes to PNG.

## How to convert an image with BISCS India

1. Open [Convert Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-converter/) and choose your files, drag them in, or paste a copied image with Ctrl + V.
2. Select the target format: **JPG**, **PNG** or **WebP**. WebP output appears if your browser can create it, which current Chrome, Edge and Firefox can.
3. For JPG and WebP, set the **Quality**. Around 85–92% keeps photos looking identical to the original while saving space.
4. If you are converting a transparent PNG to JPG, pick the **background colour** that should fill the transparent parts. White is the usual choice.
5. Download the file, or download all converted files together as a ZIP.

## Common conversions and when they make sense

### PNG to JPG

This is the most common one. Phone screenshots and some scanner apps save as PNG, which can be several megabytes for a single image. Many exam and job portals in India only accept JPG for photo and signature uploads. Converting fixes both issues in one step.

If the PNG has a transparent background, such as a signature cut-out, the transparent area must become a solid colour in JPG. Choose white for forms.

### JPG to PNG

Converting a JPG to PNG does **not** improve its quality. The compression artefacts already in the JPG stay there, and the file usually grows. It makes sense only when the next program in your workflow requires PNG, or you plan to edit the image repeatedly and do not want further JPG losses each time you save.

### Anything to WebP

If you run a website, an online shop or a blog, WebP is usually the most efficient choice for both photos and graphics, and it supports transparency. Page speed matters for visitors on mobile data, so converting your product images to WebP is a worthwhile habit.

### WebP to JPG

Images saved from websites often turn out to be WebP. When an older desktop program, a print shop or a government portal refuses the file, converting it to JPG solves the problem straight away.

## What happens to quality when you convert?

JPG and WebP are **lossy**: they discard detail the eye is unlikely to notice. The quality slider controls how much is thrown away. At very low settings you will see blocky patches in skies and smudged edges around text.

PNG is **lossless**: it stores every pixel exactly. That is why the quality slider does not apply to PNG output, and why PNG photos are large.

Converting from a lossy format to a lossless one cannot bring back lost detail. Converting the other way, PNG to JPG, loses a little each time. For important images, keep the original file and convert from that rather than converting a converted copy.

## Tips for clean conversions

- **Use the right tool for size targets.** If a form says the photo must be under a certain number of KB, use [Compress Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/), which searches for the quality that fits. Converting alone may not land on the number.
- **Check dimensions too.** Converting does not change width and height. If the portal also specifies pixels, use [Resize Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-resizer/) first.
- **Keep logos in PNG.** Converting a logo with crisp edges to JPG tends to add faint halos. PNG or WebP keep it clean.
- **Batch your work.** If you are preparing thirty product photos for a website, add them all at once and download a ZIP rather than converting one at a time.
- **Animated GIFs become still images.** The converter works on a single frame, so an animation will not survive conversion to JPG or PNG.

## Common mistakes

- Converting a JPG to PNG expecting it to look sharper. It will not, and the file will be bigger.
- Saving a transparent logo as JPG and getting a black or white box around it.
- Uploading WebP to a portal that only lists JPG and PNG, then wondering why the upload button greys out.
- Setting quality to 100% for every photo. The file grows a lot for almost no visible gain over 90%.
- Renaming a file from `.png` to `.jpg` by hand. That changes the label, not the content, and some portals will detect the mismatch.

## Is the conversion private?

Yes. The BISCS India converter uses your browser’s own image encoding, so the file is read and rewritten on your phone or computer. Nothing is uploaded, which matters if you are converting scanned certificates, ID cards or client work. When you have finished, you can turn the result into a PDF with [JPG to PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/jpg-to-pdf/) if the portal wants a document rather than an image.

Q: Does converting PNG to JPG reduce quality?
A: Slightly, because JPG uses lossy compression. At a quality of around 90% the difference is very hard to see in photos. Screenshots with sharp text can show faint smudges around letters, so keep those as PNG if crispness matters more than file size.

Q: Why did the transparent background turn white after converting to JPG?
A: JPG has no support for transparency, so every transparent pixel must be given a solid colour. The converter lets you choose that background colour. If you need to keep the transparency, convert to PNG or WebP instead, both of which support it.

Q: How do I open a WebP image that will not upload to a form?
A: Some older websites and government portals only accept JPG or PNG. Add the WebP file to the converter, choose JPG as the target format and download. The new file will open and upload anywhere that accepts ordinary photos.

Q: Can I convert HEIC iPhone photos with this tool?
A: The converter reads any image format your browser can open. Most browsers on Windows and Android cannot decode HEIC, so it may not load there. On an iPhone, sharing the photo as Most Compatible or changing the camera setting to JPG avoids the problem.

Q: Is converting the format the same as compressing the image?
A: Not exactly, but they are related. Converting a PNG photo to JPG or WebP usually makes it much smaller, because those formats compress photos better. If you need to reach a specific KB limit, use the compressor, which can search for the right quality automatically.
