## Which aspect ratio should you crop to?

An aspect ratio is simply width compared to height. Picking the right one before you crop saves you from having the platform crop your picture for you, often in the wrong place.

| Aspect ratio | Shape | Common uses |
|---|---|---|
| Free | Any | Removing clutter, trimming screenshots, documents |
| Original | Same as your photo | Tightening a shot without changing its shape |
| 1:1 | Square | Instagram posts, WhatsApp and LinkedIn profile photos, product thumbnails |
| 4:3 and 3:4 | Classic photo | Standard prints, presentations, most phone cameras |
| 3:2 | DSLR photo | 6 × 4 inch prints |
| 16:9 | Widescreen | YouTube thumbnails, slides, desktop wallpapers |
| 9:16 | Tall | Stories, Reels, Shorts, phone wallpapers |
| Passport 35:45 | Portrait | Passport and visa photos, many application forms |

If a website asks for a specific size such as 1280 × 720, that is 16:9. A request for 600 × 600 is 1:1. Matching the ratio first means the later resize will not stretch or squash anything.

## How to crop a photo step by step

1. Open [Crop Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-cropper/) and choose your photo, drop it on the page or paste it with Ctrl + V.
2. Tap an **Aspect ratio** chip, or leave it on **Free** to crop any shape.
3. Drag inside the frame to move it, and drag a corner or edge handle to resize it. The grid lines help you line up horizons and eyes using the rule of thirds.
4. For precision, type values into the **X**, **Y**, **Width** and **Height** fields. On a keyboard, the arrow keys nudge the frame and Shift + arrows resize it.
5. Check the **Result preview**, which shows the final output size in pixels.
6. Download the cropped image.

## Tips for a better crop

### Use the rule of thirds

The grid divides the frame into nine parts. Placing a person’s eyes on the upper line, or the horizon on the lower or upper line rather than the middle, tends to look more natural. For product photos and passport-style shots, centring is better.

### Leave breathing room

Cropping right up to the edge of someone’s head or chin looks cramped. Leave a little space above the head and keep the chin clear. If you are cropping for an official photo, follow the specific head-size guidance of the authority concerned.

### Watch the pixel count

Every crop throws pixels away. A tight crop from a 12-megapixel photo is still large, but a tight crop from a WhatsApp image might leave only a few hundred pixels, which will look soft when printed or enlarged. The result preview tells you the final size before you download.

### Straighten first

If the horizon is tilted, crop alone will not fix it. Straighten the photo with the fine-angle control in [Rotate & Flip Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-flip-image/), then crop away the angled edges.

## Cropping photos for application forms and ID cards

Many Indian application portals, from university admissions to recruitment exams, ask for a recent passport-style photograph with the face clearly visible and a plain light background. Before resizing and compressing to meet the portal’s limits, crop properly:

- Use **Passport 35:45** if the form describes a passport-size photograph, or the ratio implied by the dimensions in the notice.
- Keep the full face, both ears where possible, and the top of the shoulders in view.
- Make sure there is no other person, hand or object in the frame.

Then resize with [Resize Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-resizer/) and compress with [Compress Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/) to meet the exact numbers in the official notice. If you want a printable sheet of passport photos instead, the [Passport Photo Maker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/passport-photo-maker/) is purpose-built for that.

## Common cropping mistakes

- **Cropping in the wrong ratio and then forcing a resize.** The picture gets stretched. Choose the ratio first.
- **Cutting off part of the chin or hair.** Official photos are often rejected for this. Leave a margin.
- **Cropping a screenshot but leaving the status bar.** Battery and time icons look untidy in documents and presentations.
- **Over-cropping a low-resolution image.** A tiny crop from a forwarded photo will not print well.
- **Forgetting that the platform will crop again.** If you upload a 4:3 image where 1:1 is expected, the site decides what to cut. Do it yourself.

## Is it safe to crop personal photos here?

The cropping happens on your own device using your browser’s canvas. Your photo is not uploaded or stored anywhere, which is reassuring when you are trimming ID cards, certificates or family pictures. By default the output keeps the original file format, so a JPG stays a JPG, but you can switch to JPG, PNG or WebP and set the quality before downloading.

Q: Does cropping reduce the quality of a photo?
A: Cropping itself does not blur anything; it simply removes pixels outside the frame. The remaining part has fewer pixels in total, though, so if you crop a tiny area and then enlarge it for printing, it can look soft. Keep crops generous when you plan to print.

Q: How do I crop a photo to a perfect square?
A: Choose the 1:1 aspect ratio chip. The crop frame locks to a square, so however you drag the corners it stays square. Move it over your subject and download. This is ideal for Instagram posts, profile pictures and product thumbnails.

Q: Can I type exact crop coordinates?
A: Yes. Below the aspect ratio chips are X, Y, Width and Height fields in pixels. Typing values there moves and resizes the crop frame precisely, which helps when you need the same crop on several screenshots or an exact pixel size.

Q: What is the difference between cropping and resizing?
A: Cropping cuts away part of the picture and changes what is shown. Resizing keeps the whole picture but changes how many pixels it uses. For an exact size like 600 × 600, crop to the right shape first, then resize to the right dimensions.

## When do you actually need to resize a photo?

- **Online application forms.** Government recruitment portals, university admissions and bank exam sites often ask for a photo and signature within fixed pixel dimensions. Upload a full-size phone photo and the portal rejects it.

| Making an image larger | Try AI upscaling instead | Plain enlargement cannot invent missing detail |

## Understanding aspect ratio (and why photos get squashed)

The aspect ratio is the relationship between width and height. A typical phone photo is 4:3, so a 4000 × 3000 image resized to 1200 wide becomes 1200 × 900. If you then force it to 1200 × 1200, something has to give.

**Stretch** squeezes the picture into the new box, which makes people look wider or thinner. It is rarely what you want. **Crop to fill** scales the photo until the box is covered and trims the overflow from the edges. **Fit inside** scales the photo until it fits completely and fills the leftover space, so nothing is cut off.

For portraits and passport-style photos, crop to fill usually looks best. For logos, screenshots and documents, fit inside is safer because nothing important gets trimmed. If you want to choose exactly what gets trimmed, crop by hand first with [Crop Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-cropper/), then resize.

## Resizing photos for Indian exam and job application forms

Recruitment and admission portals in India commonly ask for a recent colour photograph and a scanned signature, each with its own pixel dimensions, file format and size range in KB. The exact numbers are not universal. They differ between SSC, UPSC, banking, railway and state commission notifications, and they can change from one recruitment cycle to the next.

So before resizing, open the official notification or the portal’s instructions and note three things: the pixel dimensions (if given), the file format (usually JPG) and the minimum and maximum size in KB. Then:

- Resize to the stated dimensions using pixel mode with crop to fill.
- If the result is above the KB limit, run it through the compressor with a target size.
- If it is below the minimum KB, raise the quality during compression rather than enlarging the image.

For signatures, sign in dark ink on plain white paper, photograph it in good light, crop tightly around the signature and then resize. The [Signature Maker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/signature-maker/) can also create a clean digital signature if the form accepts one.

## Practical tips for better results

- **Resize once, from the original.** Every round of resizing and re-saving a JPG loses a little quality. Keep your original and always start from it.
- **Downsizing is safe, upsizing is not.** Going from 4000 to 1200 pixels looks crisp. Going from 400 to 1200 looks blurry because the extra pixels are guessed. For enlargements, the [AI Image Upscaler](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/ai-image-upscaler/) reconstructs detail more convincingly.
- **Use even numbers for video and design work.** Some video encoders and layout systems prefer even widths and heights.
- **Mind the format.** Resizing does not change the file type. If you need a JPG from a PNG screenshot, convert it as well.
- **Large batches on a phone take longer.** Everything runs on your device, so a budget phone handling fifty 12-megapixel photos will need a little patience. A laptop is quicker for big jobs.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- Typing both width and height with the lock off and ending up with distorted faces.
- Resizing a photo to the right dimensions but forgetting the KB limit, then getting rejected anyway.
- Enlarging a small WhatsApp-forwarded photo for printing and expecting it to look sharp.
- Cropping out part of the head or chin in an application photo because crop to fill trimmed more than expected. Check the preview before downloading.
- Repeatedly editing and saving the same JPG instead of going back to the original.

## Is it safe to resize personal photos online?

Many online resizers upload your image to their server, process it there and send it back. With the BISCS India resizer, the work happens locally using your browser’s built-in canvas. Your photo, ID scan or signature is never transmitted, so there is nothing stored on someone else’s computer afterwards. Once the page has loaded, the tool continues to work even on a weak connection.

That makes it a sensible choice for Aadhaar or PAN scans, family pictures and anything else you would rather not hand over to an unknown website.

Q: Does resizing an image reduce its quality?
A: Making an image smaller usually looks fine because you are throwing away pixels you do not need. Making it larger cannot add real detail, so a small photo stretched to twice its size will look soft. For enlargements, an AI upscaler gives better results than a plain resize.

Q: What is the difference between resizing and compressing?
A: Resizing changes the pixel dimensions, for example from 4000 × 3000 to 1200 × 900. Compressing keeps the dimensions but stores the pixels more efficiently, which lowers the file size in KB. Forms often specify both, so you may need to resize first and then compress.

Q: Can I resize many photos at the same time?
A: Yes. Add several images together and the same settings are applied to each of them. With the aspect ratio lock on, every photo keeps its own shape based on the width or height you enter, and you can download them all together as a ZIP file.

Q: Why is my resized photo stretched or squashed?
A: That happens when the width and height you type do not match the original shape and the image is forced into them. Keep the lock on, or choose Crop to fill or Fit inside so the tool trims or pads the picture instead of distorting faces and text.

Q: Are my photos uploaded anywhere when I resize them?
A: No. The resizing is done by your browser on your own device using the canvas feature built into every modern browser. The images are not sent to BISCS India or any other server, which makes it suitable for ID scans and personal photos.

## How to Format and Validate JSON Online (With Error Lines)

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/format-validate-json-online/
Tool: JSON Formatter (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/)

Quick answer: To format JSON, paste it into a JSON formatter, choose an indent (2 spaces, 4 spaces or tab) and copy the pretty-printed result. If the JSON is invalid, a good formatter shows the exact line and column of the error. BISCS India's JSON Formatter does all of this in your browser, so API responses never leave your device.

A JSON formatter takes a dense block of JSON, checks that it is valid, and re-prints it with consistent indentation so you can actually read it. If something is wrong, it tells you where: the line, the column and what it expected to find.

The [JSON Formatter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/) on BISCS India does three jobs in one screen: pretty-print, validate and minify. It runs entirely in your browser, which matters when the JSON you are debugging is a live API response with names, phone numbers or order details.

## What does a JSON formatter actually do?

JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is the format almost every web API speaks, from UPI payment callbacks to weather services. Servers usually send it minified, with no spaces or line breaks, because that saves bandwidth. That is fine for machines and miserable for people.

A formatter parses the text into a data structure and prints it back out with indentation. Here is the same object before and after:

```json
{"order":{"id":"ORD-2041","city":"Kolkata","items":[{"sku":"TEA-250","qty":2}],"paid":true}}
```

```json
{
  "order": {
    "id": "ORD-2041",
    "city": "Kolkata",
    "items": [
      { "sku": "TEA-250", "qty": 2 }
    ],
    "paid": true
  }
}
```

Because the formatter has to parse the JSON first, it doubles as a validator. If parsing fails, you get an error instead of output.

## How to format JSON with BISCS India

1. Open the [JSON Formatter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/).
2. Paste your JSON into the **Input JSON** box, drop a `.json` file onto it, or use **Upload**.
3. Choose an indent from the dropdown: 2 spaces, 4 spaces or Tab. Tick **Sort keys** if you want object keys in alphabetical order.
4. Click **Format**. The output appears on the right, along with a status line showing the type (object or array), number of keys, nesting depth and size.
5. Switch the output view to **Tree** if you want to expand and collapse nested objects instead of scrolling through text.
6. Use **Copy** or **Download** to save the result. Click **Minify** if you need the compact version instead.

The tool re-validates as you type, so you can fix an error and see the green "Valid JSON" badge appear straight away.

## How do I find the error in invalid JSON?

When parsing fails, the formatter shows a red "Invalid JSON" box with a plain-English message, the line and column, and a snippet of the offending line with a caret pointing at the problem. The **Go to error** button jumps your cursor to that character in the input.

Most JSON errors come from writing JavaScript-style objects by hand. The most common ones:

- **Trailing commas.** `[1, 2, 3,]` is valid JavaScript but invalid JSON. The message reads "Trailing comma before “]”".
- **Single quotes.** JSON strings and keys must use double quotes: `"name"`, never `'name'`.
- **Unquoted keys.** `{city: "Pune"}` must be `{"city": "Pune"}`.
- **Comments.** `//` and `/* */` are not part of JSON.
- **Line breaks inside strings.** A raw newline inside quotes is not allowed; it must be written as `\n`.
- **Special values.** `undefined`, `NaN` and `Infinity` do not exist in JSON. Use `null` or a string.
- **Two values side by side.** Pasting two JSON objects one after another, as often happens with log files, gives "Unexpected … after the end of the JSON value". Wrap them in an array or validate them one at a time.

A quick test you can run in any browser console shows the difference between JavaScript and JSON:

```js
JSON.parse('{"a": 1}');   // works
JSON.parse("{'a': 1}");   // SyntaxError: single quotes
JSON.parse('{"a": 1,}');  // SyntaxError: trailing comma
```

## Pretty-print or minify: which should you use?

| Situation | Use | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Reading an API response | Pretty-print, 2 spaces | Easy to scan, compact enough on screen |
| Config file in a Git repo | Pretty-print, sorted keys | Cleaner diffs when values change |
| Sending a payload over the network | Minify | Fewer bytes per request |
| Embedding JSON in an environment variable | Minify | Must fit on one line |
| Comparing two responses | Pretty-print, sorted keys, then diff | Same order makes real changes stand out |

Sorting keys is especially useful before comparing two JSON files. Format both with **Sort keys** ticked, then paste them into the [Text Diff](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/text-diff/) tool, and only genuine differences will be highlighted.

## A note on large numbers

The tool shows a warning badge, "Large numbers may lose precision", when it sees long runs of digits. This is not a bug in the formatter. Browsers store every JSON number as a 64-bit floating point value, which can only represent integers exactly up to 9,007,199,254,740,991 (2^53 − 1).

Long numeric IDs, such as some bank reference numbers or social media post IDs, can be silently rounded when parsed. If you control the API, send such IDs as strings. If you do not, be careful about copying formatted output back into a system that needs the exact value.

## Practical tips for working with JSON

- **Use the Tree view for deep data.** GST e-invoice JSON, for example, nests seller, buyer and item details several levels deep. Collapsing branches makes it much easier to find one field.
- **Keep the Sample handy.** If you are learning JSON, click **Sample** to load a small example with objects, arrays, numbers, booleans and `null`, then try breaking it to see the error messages.
- **Validate before you deploy.** A single trailing comma in a `package.json` or a translation file can break a build. Pasting the file into a validator takes seconds.
- **Convert when a spreadsheet is the real goal.** If someone asks for "this data in Excel", run the JSON through [JSON to CSV](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/) instead of formatting it by hand.
- **Minify for production assets.** For whole files, the [CSS / HTML / JSON Minifier](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/code-minifier/) shows exactly how many bytes you saved.

## Why formatting in the browser matters for privacy

Debugging often means pasting real data: customer records, internal API tokens inside a response, or payment webhook bodies. Many online formatters send that text to their server to process it, and you have no idea whether it is logged.

The BISCS India formatter uses your browser’s built-in `JSON.parse` and `JSON.stringify`. The text never leaves your device, and the page keeps working even if your connection drops after it loads. That said, if your organisation has rules about handling production data, those rules still apply.

## Limits worth knowing

The formatter handles files up to 50 MB when loaded from disk, but very large inputs will be slower to re-validate on a phone or older laptop. The tree view stops drawing after a few thousand nodes to keep the page responsive; the text output is unaffected. And because it follows the JSON standard strictly, it will not accept JSON5 or JSONC (JSON with comments) unless you remove the extra syntax first.

Q: Why does my JSON say “Unexpected token” when it looks fine?
A: The usual culprits are a trailing comma after the last item, single quotes instead of double quotes, comments, or an unquoted key. JavaScript object syntax allows some of these, but strict JSON does not. The formatter points to the line and column so you can fix the exact character.

Q: Is it safe to paste API responses with customer data into an online JSON formatter?
A: It depends on the tool. Many websites send your text to a server. The BISCS India JSON Formatter parses and formats everything with JavaScript inside your browser, so nothing is uploaded. Even so, follow your company’s data policy for production data containing personal details.

Q: Does formatting JSON change the data?
A: No. Formatting only adds or removes whitespace between tokens. Keys, values and order stay the same, unless you tick Sort keys, which reorders object keys alphabetically. Very large integers above 2^53 may lose precision because browsers store JSON numbers as 64-bit floating point values.

Q: What is the difference between pretty-printing and minifying JSON?
A: Pretty-printing adds line breaks and indentation so people can read the structure. Minifying removes all unnecessary whitespace so the file is as small as possible for sending over a network. Both versions represent exactly the same data and parse to the same result.

Q: Can I add comments to a JSON file?
A: Standard JSON has no comment syntax, so a strict parser rejects them. Some tools accept variants such as JSONC or JSON5 for configuration files, but if the file is consumed by an API or JSON.parse, remove comments or store notes in a normal string field instead.

## How to Convert JSON to CSV for Excel (Nested Data Too)

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/convert-json-to-csv-excel/
Tool: JSON to CSV (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/)

Quick answer: To convert JSON to CSV, paste a JSON array of objects into a converter, which turns each object into a row and each key into a column. BISCS India's JSON to CSV tool also flattens nested objects into columns like address.city and adds a UTF-8 BOM so Excel shows Indian-language text correctly, all inside your browser.

To convert JSON to CSV, you need JSON shaped like a list of records: an array of objects. Each object becomes one row and each key becomes a column header. Paste it into a converter, download the `.csv`, and open it in Excel or Google Sheets.

The [JSON to CSV](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/) tool on BISCS India does this instantly in your browser. It also flattens nested objects, merges keys that only appear in some records, and adds a byte order mark so Excel does not garble Hindi names or the ₹ sign.

## When do you need to turn JSON into a spreadsheet?

Developers live in JSON, but managers, accountants and clients usually want Excel. Common situations include:

- Exporting orders or leads from an API so the sales team can filter them.
- Sharing a list of form submissions with someone who does not code.
- Reconciling payment gateway data against your books.
- Loading data into a tool that only accepts CSV imports.

CSV (comma-separated values) is the simplest common format both worlds understand. It is plain text, one record per line, with values separated by a delimiter.

## How the conversion works

Take this JSON array of customers:

```json
[
  { "id": 1, "name": "Asha Verma", "address": { "city": "Delhi", "pin": "110001" }, "tags": ["admin", "sales"] },
  { "id": 2, "name": "Rohan Das", "address": { "city": "Kolkata" }, "active": false }
]
```

With **Flatten nested objects** switched on, the converter produces:

```text
id,name,address.city,address.pin,tags,active
1,Asha Verma,Delhi,110001,"admin, sales",
2,Rohan Das,Kolkata,,,false
```

Notice three things. The nested `address` object became two columns using dot notation. The simple array `tags` became a single comma-separated value, quoted because it contains a comma. And `active`, which only Rohan’s record has, still gets a column; Asha’s cell is simply empty. The converter collects every key from every object, in the order it first sees them.

## Step-by-step: JSON to CSV with BISCS India

1. Open [JSON to CSV](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-to-csv/).
2. Paste your JSON into the left box, or click **Upload** to load a `.json` file. You can also drag a file onto the box.
3. Pick a **Delimiter**: comma, semicolon, tab or pipe.
4. Leave **Flatten nested objects (a.b.c)** ticked unless you want nested objects stored as raw JSON text in one cell.
5. Keep **Header row** ticked so the first line holds the column names.
6. Check the table under **Preview**. It shows up to the first 100 rows so you can spot problems before downloading.
7. Click **Download .csv**. With **Excel-friendly download (UTF-8 BOM)** ticked, the file opens correctly in Excel with a double-click.

If the JSON has a syntax error, the tool shows the line and column instead of output. Fix it there, or run it through the [JSON Formatter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/json-formatter/) for a fuller view.

## What if my JSON is not a simple array?

Real API responses are rarely a bare array. They tend to look like this:

```json
{ "status": "ok", "page": 1, "results": [ { "id": 1 }, { "id": 2 } ] }
```

The converter looks for exactly one array of objects inside the top-level object. If it finds one, it uses it and shows a note such as "Using the “results” array." If there are several such arrays, it cannot guess which one you mean, so it treats the whole object as one row. In that case, copy just the array you want into the input.

An array of arrays, such as `[[1, "a"], [2, "b"]]`, is also accepted. Each inner array becomes a row, with generic `column_1`, `column_2` headers.

## Common mistakes when converting JSON to CSV

- **Expecting deep nesting to flatten perfectly.** Arrays of objects, such as order line items, cannot be flattened into a single row without losing structure. They are written as JSON text inside the cell. If you need one row per line item, reshape the data first.
- **Opening the CSV by double-clicking without a BOM.** Excel may show `à¤…` style garbage instead of Hindi. Keep the BOM option on, or import via Excel’s Data tab and choose UTF-8.
- **Losing leading zeros.** PIN codes are safe as text in the CSV, but Excel may strip a leading zero from values like `0042` or turn long numbers like account numbers into scientific notation. Import those columns as Text in Excel.
- **Mixing delimiters and locale.** If Excel puts everything in column A, your regional settings probably expect semicolons. Re-download with the semicolon delimiter.
- **Forgetting that dates are just strings.** JSON has no date type, so dates come through exactly as written, for example `2026-03-31T10:00:00Z`. Format them in the spreadsheet afterwards.

## Choosing a delimiter

| Delimiter | Best for |
| --- | --- |
| Comma `,` | Default; Excel and Google Sheets in Indian and US locales |
| Semicolon `;` | Spreadsheets set to European locales |
| Tab | Pasting straight into a sheet; data full of commas |
| Pipe | Script-to-script transfers, legacy bank and ERP formats |

## Privacy: your data stays on your device

Exports of customers, employees or payments are exactly the kind of data you should not paste into random websites. This converter reads and transforms the JSON with JavaScript in your own browser. Nothing is uploaded, and the CSV is generated locally when you click download.

## Going the other way, or into Excel directly

If you later receive a CSV and need JSON for an API or a script, use [CSV to JSON](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/csv-to-json/), which also detects numbers and booleans. For converting between CSV and real `.xlsx` workbooks, the [Excel & CSV Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/excel-csv-converter/) handles the spreadsheet side.

## Tips for cleaner output

Keep key names short and consistent before converting, because they become your column headers. `customer_name` in one record and `customerName` in another will produce two separate columns. If your data comes from multiple API versions, normalise the keys first.

Finally, remember that the preview is your friend. Scroll it horizontally to check that every column you expect is there, and that nothing important ended up as a block of JSON text in a single cell.

Q: What JSON structure converts best to CSV?
A: An array of flat objects, where every object has the same keys, maps perfectly to a table: one object per row, one key per column. Nested objects can be flattened into dotted column names. Deeply nested arrays of objects do not fit a flat table well and are written as JSON text inside a cell.

Q: Why does Excel show strange characters instead of Hindi or the ₹ symbol?
A: Excel on Windows may guess the wrong text encoding when opening a CSV. Adding a UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) at the start of the file tells Excel the file is UTF-8. The BISCS India tool adds this by default when you download, so Devanagari, Bengali and ₹ display correctly.

Q: My JSON is an object, not an array. Can I still convert it?
A: Yes. If the object contains exactly one array of objects, such as a results or data field, the tool uses that array automatically and tells you which one it picked. Otherwise the single object becomes a one-row CSV with each key as a column.

Q: What happens to commas and line breaks inside values?
A: They are handled using standard CSV quoting. Any value containing the delimiter, a double quote or a line break is wrapped in double quotes, and inner quotes are doubled. Excel, Google Sheets and most programming libraries read this format correctly.

Q: Should I use a comma or semicolon delimiter?
A: Use a comma for most cases. Choose semicolon if your spreadsheet is set to a European locale where the comma is the decimal separator. Tab is useful when pasting directly into a spreadsheet, and pipe suits data that contains lots of commas and is read by scripts.

## Lorem Ipsum Generator: Free Placeholder Text for Designs

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/lorem-ipsum-placeholder-text-generator/
Tool: Lorem Ipsum Generator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/lorem-ipsum-generator/)

Quick answer: A lorem ipsum generator creates meaningless Latin-style placeholder text so you can fill a design before the real content is ready. BISCS India’s Lorem Ipsum Generator makes any number of paragraphs, sentences or words, can wrap them in HTML paragraph tags, and lets you copy or download the result instantly.

Lorem ipsum is placeholder text: scrambled Latin-looking words that fill a layout before the real content exists. Designers, developers and print shops use it to see how a page looks with text in place, without readers getting distracted by what the words say.

A lorem ipsum generator saves you hunting for the passage online. Choose how much you need, click once, and paste it into your mock-up.

## Where does lorem ipsum come from?

The text is derived from a passage in a Latin work on ethics by the Roman statesman Cicero. Over time, typesetters cut words and syllables from it until it became nonsense that still looks like a natural language, with a realistic mix of short and long words.

That realism is why it outlived alternatives like repeating "text text text" or "content goes here". Repeated words create obvious patterns on the page, and readable English pulls people into reading rather than judging spacing, fonts and hierarchy.

## How to generate lorem ipsum text

1. Open the [Lorem Ipsum Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/lorem-ipsum-generator/).
2. Choose what to generate: **Paragraphs**, **Sentences** or **Words**.
3. Enter how many you need. The defaults are 3 paragraphs, 5 sentences or 50 words.
4. Decide on the options. **Start with "Lorem ipsum…"** gives the classic opening line, and **Wrap in HTML p tags** formats each paragraph for web templates.
5. Click **Regenerate** for a fresh random version, then **Copy** or **Download** the text.

The word and character totals appear under the output, so you can match a target length, such as a 160-character meta description or a 60-word product blurb.

## When should you use placeholder text?

Lorem ipsum is the right choice when the **layout** is what you are testing. Good examples:

- **Website and app mock-ups** in Figma, Canva or plain HTML before the copy is written.
- **WordPress or Shopify theme testing**, to see how blog cards, product descriptions and footers cope with short and long text.
- **Print layouts** for brochures, menus, wedding cards and visiting cards, so the client can approve the design first.
- **Developer testing**: checking that a long paragraph wraps properly, that text does not overflow a button, and that a page still works with 10,000 words.
- **Presentation templates**, where every slide needs plausible body text.

## When real content works better

Placeholder text has real drawbacks, and experienced designers often avoid it for anything beyond early wireframes.

| Situation | Better choice | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Final client review | Real or near-final copy | Clients judge the content, not the boxes |
| Hindi, Bengali or other Indic layouts | Sample text in that script | Indic scripts need more line height and different fonts |
| Forms, buttons, error messages | Actual labels | Wording drives usability |
| Product pages | Real product names and prices | Lengths vary hugely, for example "Tea" vs a 70-character title |
| Pages going live | Never placeholder | Unfinished pages hurt trust and search visibility |

A practical middle ground is to use lorem ipsum for long body text, but real headings, button labels and prices from day one.

## Common mistakes with dummy text

- **Publishing it by accident.** It happens more often than you would think, especially in image alt text, meta descriptions and footer columns. Search for "lorem" before every launch.
- **Testing only the ideal length.** Real content is messy. Generate one very short and one very long version of each block to see how the design handles both.
- **Forgetting other languages.** If your site will serve Hindi or Tamil readers, Latin filler hides problems with font rendering and line breaks.
- **Copying from random websites.** Some "lorem ipsum" pages include hidden characters or odd formatting. A clean generator avoids that, and you can run any pasted text through the [Whitespace Cleaner](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/whitespace-cleaner/) if needed.

## Tips for designers and developers

**Match realistic lengths.** If product descriptions on your marketplace are usually 40 to 80 words, generate 60 words rather than three full paragraphs. Use the word count below the output to check.

**Use the HTML option for templates.** With **Wrap in HTML p tags** ticked, each paragraph comes inside its own HTML paragraph element, ready to paste into a code editor or the HTML view of a content management system. The download is then saved as an `.html` file.

**Preview formatted text quickly.** Writing documentation or a README? Paste generated paragraphs into the [Markdown Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/markdown-preview/) alongside some headings and lists to see the full page structure.

**Check the numbers.** When a design brief says "around 300 words per section", paste your mix of real and placeholder text into the [Word Counter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/word-counter/) to confirm.

## Lorem ipsum in Word, Docs and design apps

Some programs have their own shortcuts. In Microsoft Word, typing `=lorem()` on a new line and pressing Enter inserts placeholder paragraphs, and `=rand()` inserts readable English sample text instead. Design tools such as Figma and Canva offer plugins or built-in fillers too.

Those shortcuts are handy, but they tie you to one program and give you little control over length. A browser generator works the same way everywhere: on your office PC, on a client's laptop or on your phone while you are reviewing a layout. You decide the exact number of words or sentences, then paste the result into any app, email or code editor.

It also helps when several people work on one project. If the developer, designer and content writer all use the same generator with the same settings, a "three-paragraph block" means the same thing to everyone, and the mock-ups line up.

## A quick checklist before you hand over a design

- Every block of placeholder text is clearly marked as temporary in the brief.
- Headings, buttons, prices and form labels use real wording.
- Long and short versions of key blocks have both been tested.
- Any Indian-language sections have been checked with real text in that script.
- A final search for "lorem" and "ipsum" returns nothing on the live site.

When you are ready to replace the filler, open the [Lorem Ipsum Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/lorem-ipsum-generator/) one last time to compare lengths, so the real copy fits the space you designed for.

## Is a lorem ipsum generator free and private?

Yes. The BISCS India generator creates the text in your browser from a built-in word list, with no account, sign-up or watermark. Nothing you configure is sent to a server, and there is no limit on how many times you regenerate.

The only practical limits are per batch: up to 100 paragraphs, 1,000 sentences or 10,000 words at once, which covers almost any design or testing job.

Q: What does lorem ipsum actually mean?
A: It does not mean anything as a whole. The text is a scrambled and shortened version of a passage from a Latin work on ethics by the Roman writer Cicero, with words cut and altered so it reads as nonsense. That is the point: readers are not distracted by meaning while they judge the layout.

Q: Is it fine to publish a page that still has lorem ipsum?
A: No. Live pages with placeholder text look unfinished, confuse visitors and give search engines nothing useful to index. Before launch, search your site or document for the words lorem and ipsum to catch any blocks you missed, including image alt text and meta descriptions.

Q: Can I get placeholder text with HTML tags?
A: Yes. Tick Wrap in HTML p tags and each paragraph is placed inside its own paragraph element, ready to paste into an HTML template or a CMS code view. The download button then saves an .html file instead of a plain text file.

Q: How much placeholder text can I generate at once?
A: The generator allows up to 100 paragraphs, 1,000 sentences or 10,000 words in a single batch. That is more than enough for long-page mock-ups, print layouts or testing how a template handles very long content.

Q: Should I use lorem ipsum or Hindi placeholder text for Indian designs?
A: If the final content will be in Hindi or another Indian language, test with real sample text in that script, not Latin filler. Devanagari and other Indic scripts have different line heights, word lengths and font needs, and lorem ipsum will not reveal those problems.

## How to Merge PDF Files Online for Free (Without Uploading)

Quick answer: To merge PDF files, open a PDF merger, add two or more files, drag them into the order you want and download the combined PDF. BISCS India’s Merge PDF tool does this in your browser, so documents like bank statements and ID proofs are never uploaded to a server.

The whole job happens in your browser. Your files are read and joined on your own device and are never uploaded, which is exactly what you want when the PDFs are bank statements, Form 16s or identity documents.

## Why people merge PDFs

Almost every application in India now ends with an upload step, and many portals allow only one file per section. Merging solves that. A few typical cases:

- **Loan or credit card applications**: six months of bank statements, three salary slips and an address proof, sent as a single PDF.
- **Visa and passport paperwork**: covering letter, itinerary, hotel bookings and ITR acknowledgements in one file.
- **College admissions**: mark sheets for Class 10, Class 12 and each semester combined into one "educational documents" upload.
- **Office reporting**: weekly reports from different branches joined into one pack for the regional manager.
- **Tax filing**: Form 16, Form 26AS and investment proofs bundled for your CA.

## How to merge PDFs step by step

1. Open [Merge PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/merge-pdf/) and choose your files. You can select several at once or drag them into the box.
2. Add more files any time using the **Add more PDFs** area.
3. Arrange the order. Drag a file by its handle, or use the arrow buttons. Files are merged from top to bottom.
4. Remove any file you added by mistake.
5. Click the merge button. A progress bar shows each file being added.
6. Download the merged PDF. The result screen shows the total pages and how many files were joined.

## A checklist before you merge

Getting the order and contents right first saves you from redoing the job.

- Rename files with numbers (01-cover, 02-statement, 03-payslip) so they are easy to sort.
- Rotate any sideways scans first with [Rotate PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-pdf/), because pages are merged exactly as they are.
- Delete blank or irrelevant pages before merging, or afterwards with [Remove PDF Pages](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/).
- Fill in any interactive forms before merging, since form fields are not carried over.
- Check whether the portal has a file size limit, and keep an eye on the total size of what you are adding.

## Government portal uploads: size and format

Indian government and institutional portals often set a maximum file size per upload, and the limit varies a great deal between portals and even between sections of the same form. Some accept only a few hundred KB, others a few MB. There is no single national rule, so always read the instructions on the specific portal you are using.

Merging never makes files smaller; the merged PDF is roughly the sum of its parts. If you go over the limit, run the result through [Compress PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/). For scanned documents, the Strong level usually brings the size down a lot while keeping text readable.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Wrong order.** Reviewers rarely search through a file. Put the most important document first, or follow the order the portal lists.
- **Mixing portrait and landscape carelessly.** It is fine to combine them, but make sure each page is upright.
- **Merging locked PDFs.** Password-protected files are flagged with an "encrypted" label in the file list. Save an unlocked copy first.
- **Merging photos instead of PDFs.** If some documents are JPG photos from your phone, convert them with [Images to PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/jpg-to-pdf/) first, then merge.
- **Expecting bookmarks to survive.** Outline bookmarks and form fields are dropped. The pages themselves are untouched.

## Merge vs organise: which tool do you need?

| You want to… | Use |
|---|---|
| Join whole files end to end | Merge PDF |
| Join files and then move individual pages around, rotate or delete some | Organize PDF (it has an "Add PDF" button) |
| Take a few pages from one file into a new file | Extract PDF Pages |

Merge is the quickest when each file already contains the right pages in the right order. If you need page-by-page control, start with [Organize PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/organize-pdf/) instead.

## Tips for large batches

On a phone, merging ten small PDFs takes a few seconds. Very large scanned files, such as a 100-page property document, need more memory. If your phone struggles, try a laptop, close other heavy tabs, or merge in two stages: combine half the files, then merge that result with the rest.

The merged file is named after the first PDF with "-merged" added. Rename it to something meaningful, like `Rahul-Sharma-KYC-documents.pdf`, before uploading, because reviewers see the filename.

## Your files stay private

Many free PDF websites upload your documents, process them on their servers and then delete them, or say they do. With browser-based processing there is nothing to delete, because nothing was sent. The page loads the PDF library once, and from then on the merging happens on your device, even if your connection drops midway.

Q: Is it safe to merge confidential PDFs online?
A: It is safe with a tool that processes files locally. BISCS India’s Merge PDF reads and joins the files inside your browser, so nothing is sent to a server. With upload-based sites, your documents pass through someone else’s computer, which is worth avoiding for KYC papers, payslips and legal documents.

Q: How many PDFs can I merge at once?
A: There is no fixed number. You need at least two files, and you can keep adding more. The practical limit is your device’s memory, so dozens of large scanned PDFs may be slow on an older phone. On a laptop, merging fifty or more ordinary files is usually fine.

Q: Will merging reduce the quality of my PDFs?
A: No. Pages are copied into the new file as they are, keeping their original size, orientation, text and images. Nothing is re-compressed. If the merged file turns out too large for an upload portal, compress it afterwards as a separate step.

Q: Can I merge password-protected PDFs?
A: Encrypted files are flagged when you add them, and the pages may not come out correctly. Open the protected PDF with its password in a PDF reader, save or print an unprotected copy, and merge that copy instead.

Q: Are bookmarks and form fields kept after merging?
A: No. The merged PDF keeps every page exactly as it looks, but bookmarks (the outline panel) and interactive form fields from the original files are not carried over. Fill any forms before merging if you need the values to appear.

## Meta Tag Generator: Write Title, Description and OG Tags

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/meta-tag-generator-title-description-og-tags/
Tool: Meta Tag Generator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/meta-tag-generator/)

Quick answer: A meta tag generator turns your page title, description, URL and share image into ready-to-paste HTML for the head of your page. BISCS India's free Meta Tag Generator builds the title, meta description, robots, canonical, Open Graph and X (Twitter) tags in your browser and warns you about lengths and common errors.

A meta tag generator saves you from hand-typing the dozen or so lines of HTML that tell search engines and social apps what a page is about. You fill in a title, a short description, the page URL and a share image, and it gives you correctly formatted tags to paste into the `<head>` of the page.

The [Meta Tag Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/meta-tag-generator/) from BISCS India does this live as you type. It also measures your title and description in approximate pixels, flags missing or broken values, and leaves out tags that no longer matter.

## What are meta tags, and which ones still matter?

Meta tags are lines of HTML that describe a page rather than appear on it. Visitors rarely see them directly, but Google, Bing, WhatsApp and LinkedIn all read them when they display your link.

Not every tag is worth adding. Here is what the generator produces and why:

| Tag | What it does | Still useful? |
|---|---|---|
| `<title>` | The clickable headline in search results and the browser tab | Essential |
| `meta name="description"` | Often used as the snippet under the title | Very useful for clicks |
| `meta name="robots"` | Tells search engines whether to index the page and follow links | Useful, especially to avoid accidental noindex |
| `link rel="canonical"` | Names the main version of a page when duplicates exist | Important for sites with filters, tracking links or www/non-www versions |
| `og:title`, `og:description`, `og:image` | Controls link previews on Facebook, WhatsApp and LinkedIn | Essential if links get shared |
| `twitter:card` | Chooses a large-image or small card on X | Worth adding |
| `meta charset` and `viewport` | Correct text encoding and mobile layout | Essential basics |
| `meta name="keywords"` | Once listed target keywords | Ignored by Google, so left out |

The tool also offers optional extras such as `theme-color` (the colour some mobile browsers use for the address bar), an author tag, `og:locale` from the language you choose, and `max-image-preview:large`, which permits search engines to show a large image preview of your page.

## How to generate meta tags with the BISCS tool

1. Open the [Meta Tag Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/meta-tag-generator/). Press **Sample** first if you want to see a filled-in example.
2. Type your **page title**. Watch the counter and colour bar: it shows characters and an estimated pixel width, and turns amber or red when the title is likely to be cut off.
3. Write a **meta description** of one or two sentences. The counter aims you at roughly 120–160 characters.
4. Add the **canonical URL** and **site name**. The URL must be a full address starting with `https://`.
5. Paste a **share image URL** (1200 × 630 px is the recommended size) and add **image alt text**.
6. Choose the **language** (English (India), Hindi, Bengali, Tamil and other Indian languages are listed), the **page type** (website, article or profile) and the **X card type**.
7. Check the **Robots & technical** boxes. Leave "Allow indexing" ticked unless you really want the page hidden from search.
8. Read any warnings under the output, then press **Copy** or **Download** and paste the tags into your page's `<head>`.

Everything runs in your browser. Nothing you type is sent to a server, so you can draft tags for an unreleased product page without it leaking anywhere.

## How to write a title that gets clicked

The title tag is still one of the strongest on-page signals, and it is the first thing a searcher reads. A few habits make a real difference:

- **Lead with the topic.** "GST Calculator – Free CGST, SGST and IGST Split" beats "Welcome to Sharma & Associates | Home".
- **Keep it within the visible width.** Google cuts titles by pixels, roughly 600 px on desktop. Wide letters like W and M use more space than i and l, which is why the tool shows pixel estimates.
- **Make every title unique.** Ten pages called "Services | Company Name" compete with each other.
- **Add the brand at the end** if there is room, separated by a pipe or dash.
- **Avoid shouting.** ALL CAPS and stacks of exclamation marks look spammy and take more width.

## Writing a meta description people actually read

Google does not use the meta description as a ranking factor, but it often shows it as the snippet, and a good snippet earns more clicks. Think of it as a short advert for the page.

A practical formula is: what the page offers, who it is for, and one reason to choose it. For example, a Kolkata coaching centre might write: "Weekend JEE Main crash course in Salt Lake with small batches, printed notes and weekly mock tests. See fees and batch timings."

If you write it and Google still shows something else, that is normal. Google picks text that best matches each search. A clear, accurate description simply improves the odds that yours is used.

## Open Graph tags and WhatsApp previews

In India, a large share of links are shared on WhatsApp before anyone searches for them. When someone pastes your URL into a chat, WhatsApp reads the `og:title`, `og:description` and `og:image` tags to build the preview card.

Without them, the app guesses, and you might get a blank grey box or your cookie banner text. With them, you get a proper card with your image and headline. Use an absolute image URL (starting with `https://`), keep the file reasonably small, and stick to the 1.91:1 shape so it is not awkwardly cropped.

To check how a card will look before publishing, paste the same details into the [Social Share Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/social-share-preview/) tool.

## Common meta tag mistakes

- **Leaving noindex on after launch.** Developers often block staging sites. If that tag reaches the live site, the page disappears from Google. The generator warns you when indexing is switched off.
- **Relative image paths.** `og:image` set to `/images/banner.jpg` fails on most social networks. Use the full URL.
- **Canonical pointing to the wrong page.** Copying a template and forgetting to update the canonical tells Google that every page is a duplicate of the home page.
- **Duplicate titles across a site.** Common on e-commerce category pages and blog archives.
- **Stuffing keywords into the title.** "Cheap Shoes, Buy Shoes Online, Best Shoes India" reads badly and rarely helps.
- **Forgetting alt text for the share image.** It helps screen reader users when the image appears in feeds.

## When should you use a meta tag generator?

It is most useful when you are building or fixing pages by hand: a static HTML site, a landing page for a Diwali offer, a college fest microsite, or a template you will reuse. If you use WordPress with an SEO plugin, the plugin fills these fields for you, but the generator is still handy for drafting titles and descriptions and checking their length before you paste them in.

After publishing, run the page through the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/) to confirm the tags are actually present in the final HTML, and use the [Google SERP Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/serp-preview/) to fine-tune how the result looks on mobile and desktop. If you are adding structured data too, the [Schema Markup Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/schema-markup-generator/) creates the matching JSON-LD.

Good meta tags will not rescue a weak page, but they make sure a good page is described properly everywhere it appears. Draft yours in the [Meta Tag Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/meta-tag-generator/), paste them in, and check the result once the page is live.

Q: Does Google still use the meta keywords tag?
A: No. Google has said for many years that it ignores the meta keywords tag for ranking, which is why the BISCS generator leaves it out. Spend that effort on a clear title, a useful description and good content on the page instead.

Q: Why does Google show a different description from the one I wrote?
A: Google rewrites snippets when it thinks other text on the page better matches the search. A description that accurately summarises the page and includes the main topic is more likely to be used, but there is no way to force it.

Q: How long should a meta description be?
A: Around 120–160 characters is a sensible target. Google truncates by pixel width rather than a fixed character count, so the generator shows both the character count and an estimated pixel width, and warns you when the text is likely to be cut off.

Q: Do I need separate Open Graph and Twitter tags?
A: Open Graph tags are read by Facebook, WhatsApp and LinkedIn, and X can fall back to them. Adding the twitter:card tag is still worthwhile because it tells X whether to show a large image card or a small summary.

Q: Where do I paste the generated meta tags?
A: Inside the head section of your page’s HTML, before the closing head tag. On WordPress or a site builder, use the SEO plugin or page settings fields instead of editing the theme, so updates do not overwrite your changes.

## Everyday situations where a quick edit helps

**Filling a non-fillable form.** Many college admission forms, society NOC letters and older bank forms are scanned PDFs with no typing fields. Use Add text for your details and Tick for checkboxes, then print or email the result.

**Correcting an invoice before sending.** Spotted that the invoice says "Kolkata 700019" when it should be 700091? Edit text fixes the line without regenerating the whole document. For amounts, type "Rs." rather than the ₹ symbol, because the standard PDF fonts do not include it.

**Reviewing a draft.** A manager in Pune can highlight clauses, circle a figure and add a short comment, then send the file back on WhatsApp or email.

**Adding a company stamp or logo.** Upload a PNG of your stamp with the Image tool and place it next to the signature line.

## Edit text vs Add text vs Whiteout

| Tool | What it does | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Edit text | Covers an existing line and replaces it with your new text | Fixing typos, dates, names, numbers |
| Add text | Places new text anywhere | Filling blanks, adding notes |
| Whiteout | Draws a white box over content | Hiding stray marks or old details visually |

The key point: **Edit text and Whiteout hide content visually; they do not erase it from the file.** Someone with the right software may still be able to select or extract the covered text. For truly confidential redaction (for example, hiding an account number before sharing a statement publicly), recreate the document from its source or use dedicated redaction software.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Using Indian-language text or the ₹ sign.** The editor uses standard PDF fonts, which cover English and Western characters only. Unsupported characters are replaced with "?" when you save, and the tool warns you if this happens.
- **Treating whiteout as secure deletion.** As above, it is a visual cover only.
- **Editing a password-protected PDF.** The editor cannot open locked files. Open the PDF with its password in a reader, save an unprotected copy, and edit that.
- **Forgetting to check every page.** Scroll through the thumbnails before downloading so nothing lands on the wrong page.
- **Overwriting your only copy.** Keep the original until you have checked the edited version.

## Practical tips for neat results

- Zoom in to 150% or more when placing text on narrow form lines. It is much easier to line things up.
- Match the existing font roughly: Times for formal letters and government forms, Helvetica for modern documents, Courier for typewriter-style forms.
- Use the colour picker sparingly. Black or dark blue looks most natural on official documents.
- Duplicate an item (Ctrl+D) when you need the same text or tick in several places.
- If the PDF is a phone photo of a paper form, consider making a clean copy first with [Scan to PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/), which straightens and sharpens the page.

## When should you use a different tool?

If the PDF has real form fields (you can click into boxes in a PDF reader), [Fill PDF Form](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/fill-pdf-form/) is faster and fills the actual fields. If you want to rewrite whole paragraphs, convert the file with [PDF to Word](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-to-word/), edit it there, and export a fresh PDF. And if you only need to delete or reorder pages rather than change their content, a page tool is simpler.

## Privacy: your PDF stays on your device

Most free online editors ask you to upload the document to their servers. This one does not. The page loads the editing code into your browser, and from then on all rendering and saving happens on your own phone or computer. Nothing is stored after you close the tab, which is the sensible way to handle ID proofs, payslips and contracts.

The trade-off is that your device does the work. A 200-page scanned report will open more slowly on a budget phone than on a laptop, but your data never leaves your hands.

Q: Can I change the existing text in a PDF?
A: You can replace a line of existing text. The Edit text tool covers the original line with a white box and places your new text on top in a matching standard font. It is ideal for fixing a typo, a date or an amount, but it is not the same as reflowing a whole paragraph in a word processor.

Q: Does whiteout permanently delete the text underneath?
A: No. Whiteout covers content visually, but the original text can still exist in the file and may be copied or found by search. If you need to remove sensitive information for good, do not rely on whiteout alone; recreate the document or use proper redaction software.

Q: Can I type in Hindi or Bengali on a PDF?
A: Not with this editor at the moment. It uses the standard PDF fonts (Helvetica, Times and Courier), which cover English and common Western characters. Symbols such as the rupee sign and Indian scripts are replaced with a question mark when saving, so write Rs. instead of the rupee symbol.

Q: Will editing reduce the quality of my PDF?
A: No. Your additions are drawn into the original PDF, so the existing text stays selectable and vector content stays sharp. The pages are not converted into images, which also keeps the file size close to the original.

Q: Is there a page or file size limit?
A: There is no fixed limit set by the tool because everything runs in your browser. Very long or image-heavy PDFs simply need more memory, so they open more slowly on older phones. A laptop or desktop handles large files more comfortably.

## How to Calculate Percentages: Formulas, Examples and a Free Tool

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/how-to-calculate-percentage-easily/
Tool: Percentage Calculator (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/)

Quick answer: To find a percentage of a number, multiply the number by the percentage and divide by 100: 15% of 2,400 is 2,400 × 15 ÷ 100 = 360. For percentage change, divide the difference by the original value and multiply by 100. BISCS India's free Percentage Calculator handles six common percentage questions instantly.

Percentages answer one question: how big is one number compared with another, if the whole is 100? To find X% of a number, multiply the number by X and divide by 100. To find what percent one number is of another, divide the part by the whole and multiply by 100.

That covers most everyday needs, from exam marks and salary hikes to sale discounts and GST. The rest of this guide shows the formulas for each situation, with worked examples you can check in the free [Percentage Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/).

## What are the basic percentage formulas?

Almost every percentage problem is a rearrangement of one relationship: **part = whole × percent ÷ 100**. Knowing which of the three values you are missing tells you which formula to use.

| What you want | Formula | Example |
|---|---|---|
| X% of a number | number × X ÷ 100 | 15% of 2,400 = 360 |
| What % is A of B | A ÷ B × 100 | 360 of 1,200 = 30% |
| Percentage change | (new − old) ÷ old × 100 | 50,000 to 65,000 = +30% |
| Increase by X% | value × (1 + X ÷ 100) | 1,000 + 18% = 1,180 |
| Decrease by X% | value × (1 − X ÷ 100) | 2,999 − 20% = 2,399.20 |
| A is P% of what | A ÷ P × 100 | 45 is 30% of 150 |
| Percentage difference | difference ÷ average × 100 | 80 and 120 = 40% |

The last row trips people up. Percentage *difference* compares two values with no "before" or "after", so it divides by their average. Percentage *change* has a clear starting point and divides by that.

## How do I use the BISCS Percentage Calculator?

The tool shows six small calculators on one page, each written as a plain sentence, so you never have to remember which formula applies.

1. Open the [Percentage Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) in any browser, on a phone or computer.
2. Find the card that matches your question, such as "What is __% of __?" or "Percentage change".
3. Type your numbers into the boxes. Commas are fine, so 1,25,000 and 125000 both work.
4. Read the answer in the highlighted box. A small line beside it shows the working, for example "15% × 2,400".
5. For increase or decrease, use the toggle above the boxes to switch direction.

Results update as you type, and nothing is sent anywhere. The calculations run on your device, so salary or business figures stay private.

## Worked examples from everyday life in India

### Salary hike

Your monthly salary is ₹42,000 and you are offered an 8% increment. 8% of 42,000 is 3,360, so the new salary is ₹45,360. In the tool, use "Increase or decrease by %" with 42,000 and 8.

### Exam marks

You scored 437 out of 500. 437 ÷ 500 × 100 = 87.4%. Use "What percent is X of Y" with 437 and 500. Some universities convert CGPA to percentage using their own multiplier, so check your institution's rule for official forms.

### Sale discount

A kurta priced at ₹2,999 is on 20% off. The discount is ₹599.80 and you pay ₹2,399.20. For stacked offers like "20% + extra 10%", apply them one after the other: 2,399.20 less 10% is ₹2,159.28, which is a total discount of 28%, not 30%. The [Discount Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/discount-calculator/) handles these in one go.

### Price before GST

A bill shows ₹1,180 including 18% GST and you want the pre-tax price. The final amount is 118% of the base, so the base is 1,180 ÷ 118 × 100 = ₹1,000. Use the "X is P% of what?" card with 1,180 and 118. For full CGST and SGST splits, the [GST Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/gst-calculator/) is quicker.

### Business growth

Monthly sales moved from ₹50,000 to ₹65,000. The change is 15,000 ÷ 50,000 × 100 = +30%. If you want the yearly growth rate over several years, a [CAGR Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/cagr-calculator/) is the right tool, because simple percentage change ignores compounding.

## Common percentage mistakes to avoid

- **Using the wrong base.** A fall from 120 to 80 is −33.33%, but a rise from 80 to 120 is +50%. Always divide by the starting value.
- **Assuming rises and falls cancel.** ₹1,000 up 50% is ₹1,500; down 50% from there is ₹750, not ₹1,000.
- **Adding stacked discounts.** "20% + 10% off" is a 28% total discount, because the second discount applies to a smaller price.
- **Mixing up percent and percentage points.** A home loan rate going from 6.5% to 7% is a rise of 0.5 percentage points, which is about 7.7% in relative terms.
- **Removing GST by subtracting 18%.** Taking 18% off ₹1,180 gives ₹967.60, which is wrong. Divide by 1.18 instead to get ₹1,000.
- **Confusing profit margin and markup.** A product bought at ₹800 and sold at ₹1,000 has a 25% markup on cost but a 20% margin on the selling price. The [Profit Margin Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/) shows both.

## Mental maths shortcuts worth knowing

You can do many percentages in your head with a few tricks:

- **10%** is the number divided by 10. 10% of 3,450 is 345.
- **5%** is half of 10%. So 5% of 3,450 is 172.50.
- **1%** is the number divided by 100. Build other rates from it: 18% is 10% + 5% + 3 × 1%.
- **Swap the numbers.** X% of Y equals Y% of X. 8% of 50 is the same as 50% of 8, which is 4.
- **25% and 50%** are a quarter and a half, and 20% is a fifth.

These are handy for quick checks at a shop counter. For anything that matters, such as an invoice, a loan comparison or official marks, confirm the figure with a calculator.

## When should you use a percentage calculator?

Mental maths is fine for round numbers. A calculator earns its place when:

- the numbers have decimals or are large, such as ₹18,47,250;
- you need to work backwards, such as finding the original price;
- you are comparing two values and need to know which to divide by;
- you want a quick check before sending a quotation, salary letter or report.

The BISCS tool also shows the working next to each answer, which makes it useful for students learning the method, not just for getting a number.

## Tips for accurate results

- Keep full precision until the final step. Rounding 33.333% to 33% early can shift a large total noticeably.
- When reporting change, say what it is relative to: "sales rose 30% compared with April".
- For money, round only the final amount to two decimal places.
- If the starting value is zero, percentage change is undefined. The tool warns you instead of showing a misleading figure.

Percentages are simple once you know which number is the whole. Bookmark the [Percentage Calculator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/percentage-calculator/) for the moments when you would rather not work it out on paper.

Q: How do I calculate the percentage of marks?
A: Divide the marks you scored by the maximum marks and multiply by 100. For example, 437 out of 500 is 437 ÷ 500 × 100 = 87.4%. If your board or university uses a different method, such as best-of-five subjects or CGPA conversion, follow their official rule instead.

Q: What is the difference between percentage and percentage points?
A: Percentage points describe the simple gap between two percentages, while percentage change describes the relative change. If a loan rate moves from 6.5% to 7%, it rose by 0.5 percentage points, but that is a relative increase of about 7.7% on the original rate.

Q: Why does a 50% rise followed by a 50% fall not bring me back to the start?
A: Because the second percentage is applied to a different base. ₹1,000 rising 50% becomes ₹1,500, and a 50% fall on ₹1,500 removes ₹750, leaving ₹750. Each percentage is always a share of the value it is applied to at that moment.

Q: How do I find the original price before a percentage was added?
A: Divide the final amount by (1 + rate ÷ 100). If a price including 18% GST is ₹1,180, the original is 1,180 ÷ 1.18 = ₹1,000. In the calculator, use the “X is P% of what?” box and enter 1,180 and 118.

Q: Is the percentage calculator free and private?
A: Yes. The calculator is free to use without sign-up, and all the arithmetic happens in your browser as you type. The numbers you enter are not sent to a server, so you can use it for salary, marks or business figures without worry.

## How to Delete Pages from a PDF for Free in Your Browser
