To delete pages from a PDF, open [Remove PDF Pages](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/), click the pages you want to get rid of (or type them, like `2, 5-7`), and click **Remove pages**. You get a new PDF without those pages, and your original file stays as it was.

No software, no account and no upload. The work happens in your browser, which keeps personal documents on your own device.

## When removing pages is the right fix

Most PDFs we receive carry pages we do not need. Removing them makes documents shorter, smaller and easier for the next person to read. Common cases:

- **Blank pages from double-sided scanning.** Scanners and photocopiers often add an empty back page after every sheet.
- **Terms and conditions pages.** Bank and insurance PDFs often end with several pages of fine print that a reviewer does not need.
- **Duplicate pages.** It happens when you scan the same sheet twice or merge overlapping files.
- **Sensitive pages.** Sharing a property document with a contractor? Drop the pages with family details or financial information.
- **Cover pages and adverts.** Some e-statements include promotional pages that only bulk up the file.

## How to remove pages step by step

1. Open [Remove PDF Pages](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/) and choose your PDF.
2. Wait for the page thumbnails to load.
3. Click each page you want to remove. Selected pages are marked clearly, and a counter shows how many will go.
4. Alternatively, type the pages in the **Pages to remove** box, such as `1, 3, 10-12`. The thumbnails stay in sync with what you type.
5. Read the status line: it tells you how many pages the new PDF will have.
6. Click **Remove pages** and download the new file.

## Remove, extract or split: which do you need?

These three tools overlap, so pick the one that matches how you think about the job.

| Your situation | Best tool |
|---|---|
| "I want everything except these few pages" | Remove PDF Pages |
| "I only need these few pages" | [Extract PDF Pages](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/extract-pdf-pages/) |
| "I want this document cut into several files" | [Split PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/split-pdf/) |
| "I want to delete some pages and reorder the rest" | [Organize PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/organize-pdf/) |

Removing two pages from a 50-page file is faster here; keeping two pages out of 50 is faster with Extract.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Confusing printed page numbers with PDF positions.** If page 1 of the PDF is a cover, the page printed as "3" might be the fourth page in the file. Go by the thumbnails, not the numbers in the footer.
- **Deleting a page with a signature or stamp.** Some agreements are only valid with every signed page attached. Check before removing anything from a legal document.
- **Not checking the result.** Open the downloaded file and scroll through it quickly. It takes ten seconds and avoids sending an incomplete document.
- **Overwriting the only copy.** The tool never changes your original, but if you then delete the original from your phone yourself, the removed pages are gone for good.

## Removing pages before a portal upload

When an application portal limits file size, removing unnecessary pages is often the easiest way to get under the limit without lowering quality. A scanned page can easily be several hundred KB, so dropping three blank pages may be all you need.

Limits differ from portal to portal (and sometimes between documents on the same portal), so read the specific instructions. If the file is still too big after removing pages, use [Compress PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) on the result.

## A note on sensitive information

Removing a page really removes it: the new PDF is built only from the pages you keep, so the deleted pages are not hidden inside. That makes page removal a safer way to withhold information than covering it with a white box.

However, information on the pages you keep stays as it is. If a page you need contains one sensitive line, such as a full account number, removing the page is not an option. In that case, recreate the document from its source, or use proper redaction software that permanently removes the text.

## Tips for working faster

- Zoom out in your browser (Ctrl and minus) to see more thumbnails at once in long documents.
- Use ranges for patterns. To drop the last ten pages of a 60-page file, type `51-60`.
- If every other page is blank (a common double-sided scanning result), list them as ranges or click them one by one; then confirm the count before saving.
- On mobile, tapping thumbnails is usually quicker than typing.

## Private by design

The PDF is opened by a library running inside your browser tab. Selecting pages, building the new file and saving it all happen on your device, and nothing is uploaded or stored on a server. The first visit downloads the tool's code; after that, the processing needs no internet connection at all.

Q: Can I delete pages from a PDF without Adobe Acrobat?
A: Yes. A browser-based tool can remove pages without any paid software. Open the PDF, select the pages to delete and download the result. It works on Windows, Mac, Android and iPhone in any modern browser, with no installation or account.

Q: Can I undo a page deletion?
A: The tool creates a new file and leaves your original PDF untouched on your device. If you removed the wrong page, simply start again from the original. That is also why it is a good habit to keep the original until you have checked the new version.

Q: Why can’t I remove all pages?
A: A PDF needs at least one page to be a valid document, so the tool asks you to keep at least one. If you want to discard the entire file, just delete it from your device instead.

Q: Does removing pages make the PDF smaller?
A: Usually, yes. The removed pages and their images are not copied into the new file, so the size drops roughly in proportion. Removing a few scanned pages from a large document can noticeably reduce the size before you upload it.

Q: How do I select many pages quickly?
A: Type them in the box using commas and hyphens, for example 1, 4-9, 15. The thumbnails update to match. You can also click thumbnails directly, which is easier when you are spotting blank or duplicate pages by eye.

## How to Rotate, Flip or Straighten a Photo Online for Free

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/rotate-flip-image-online-free/
Tool: Rotate & Flip Image (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-flip-image/)

Quick answer: To rotate or flip a photo, open an image rotator, press Rotate left, Rotate right or 180°, use Flip horizontal or vertical to mirror it, and download. BISCS India’s Rotate & Flip Image tool also straightens tilted photos by up to 45° and runs in your browser without uploading anything.

Rotating a photo turns it around its centre, usually by 90° or 180°, while flipping mirrors it from left to right or top to bottom. Together they fix the most common annoyances with phone pictures: sideways shots, upside-down scans, reversed selfies and slightly crooked horizons.

The [Rotate & Flip Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-flip-image/) tool from BISCS India does all of this with single clicks, plus a fine straightening slider. It works in your browser, so your photo never leaves your device.

## Why do photos end up sideways in the first place?

When you take a picture, your phone records which way it was held. Rather than rotating the pixels, many phones save them in the sensor’s natural orientation and add a small piece of metadata, the EXIF orientation tag, telling apps how to display it.

Your gallery app reads that tag and shows the photo correctly. But some websites, older desktop programs, document portals and print kiosks ignore it. The result: a photo that looked fine on your phone appears sideways after upload.

The fix is to rotate the photo and save a fresh copy, so the correct orientation is part of the image itself rather than a hint in its metadata.

## How to rotate or flip an image

1. Open [Rotate & Flip Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-flip-image/) and choose a photo, drag it in, or paste it with Ctrl + V.
2. Use **Rotate left** or **Rotate right** to turn it by 90°, or **Rotate 180°** for upside-down images.
3. Use **Flip horizontal** to mirror it left to right, or **Flip vertical** to mirror it top to bottom.
4. If the horizon or a document edge is slightly tilted, drag the **Straighten (fine angle)** slider, which moves in half-degree steps between −45° and +45°.
5. Check the output size shown under the preview. Choose the format and quality if you want something other than the original format.
6. Press **Reset** to start again at any point, or download when you are happy.

## Rotate or flip: which do you need?

| Problem | Fix | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Photo is lying on its side | Rotate left or right | One click in the correct direction |
| Scan or photo is upside down | Rotate 180° | Common with documents scanned face-down |
| Selfie text reads backwards | Flip horizontal | Restores the real-world view |
| Reflection in water or glass shot | Flip vertical | Creative use, rarely needed for fixes |
| Horizon tilts a few degrees | Straighten slider | Then crop the angled edges |
| Design needs a mirrored version | Flip horizontal | For left and right versions of a banner |

## Straightening a crooked photo the right way

A small tilt, even two or three degrees, makes buildings look like they are leaning and the sea look like it is draining off one side of the frame. To straighten:

- Find a line that should be level or vertical: a horizon, a door frame, the edge of a table, the top of a document.
- Move the slider until that line is parallel with the edge of the preview.
- Because the picture has turned, the corners of the frame now contain empty space. Use [Crop Image](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-cropper/) to trim those angled edges away.

Fine rotation resamples the pixels, so there is a very slight softening. For exact 90° turns and flips there is no such loss.

## Practical uses in everyday life

- **Documents for upload.** A photographed Aadhaar card, mark sheet or rent agreement that appears sideways on a portal looks careless and may be harder for the reviewer to read. Rotate it upright before converting it with [JPG to PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/jpg-to-pdf/).
- **Scanned PDFs.** If the problem is a page inside a PDF rather than an image, [Rotate PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-pdf/) fixes pages without converting them.
- **Mirror selfies.** Your name on a T-shirt or a shop sign behind you reading backwards is a giveaway. One horizontal flip fixes it.
- **Product photography.** Online sellers sometimes need left- and right-facing versions of the same product image for a layout. Flipping gives you both in seconds.
- **Old family photos.** Scans of prints are often slightly crooked on the scanner bed. Straighten, crop and then improve them with the [Photo Enhancer](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/ai-photo-enhancer/).

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Flipping when you meant to rotate.** A flipped portrait looks subtly wrong because faces are not perfectly symmetrical, and any text becomes mirrored. If you only wanted the photo upright, use rotate.
- **Rotating a photo that only looks wrong in one app.** If it appears correctly in your gallery but sideways on one website, the website is ignoring the orientation tag. Saving a rotated copy here fixes it everywhere.
- **Straightening without cropping.** The angled empty corners look odd in the final image.
- **Mirroring photos with logos or text for official use.** Mirrored certificates and ID documents will not be accepted.
- **Repeated JPG saves.** Rotate once, from the original, rather than saving and re-rotating a JPG many times.

## Is it private?

Yes. All the turning, flipping and straightening happens on your device using your browser’s canvas. The image is not sent anywhere, so it is fine for personal photos and documents. On older phones, very large photos may take a moment longer to save, simply because the work is done locally.

Q: Why does my photo appear sideways after uploading it?
A: Phones often store the picture in one orientation and add a small EXIF tag telling apps to turn it. Some websites ignore that tag, so the photo shows sideways. Rotating it properly and saving a new copy bakes the correct orientation into the pixels themselves.

Q: What is the difference between rotating and flipping?
A: Rotating turns the whole picture around its centre, like turning a printed photo on a table. Flipping mirrors it, so the left side becomes the right side or the top becomes the bottom. Text reads backwards after a horizontal flip, which is how you spot a mirrored selfie.

Q: Why do my selfies look reversed and how do I fix it?
A: Many front cameras show a mirror image in the preview, and some also save it that way. Writing on clothes or signs then appears backwards. Use Flip horizontal once to mirror the photo back so it matches how other people see you.

Q: Does rotating a photo lose quality?
A: Turning by exact 90 degree steps or flipping moves pixels without blending them, so the picture stays sharp. Small straightening angles require the pixels to be resampled, which softens the image very slightly. Saving as JPG also applies normal compression, so keep quality high.

## Google SERP Preview: Check Title and Snippet Before You Publish

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/google-serp-snippet-preview-tool/
Tool: Google SERP Preview (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/serp-preview/)

Quick answer: A SERP preview shows how a page’s title, URL and meta description are likely to appear in Google before you publish. BISCS India’s free Google SERP Preview renders desktop and mobile results side by side, estimates pixel widths, bolds your focus keyword and warns when text will be cut off.

A SERP preview (search engine results page preview) shows you what your listing will roughly look like in Google before the page goes live. It answers a simple but important question: will my title and description fit, and will they make someone want to click?

The [Google SERP Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/serp-preview/) on BISCS India draws a desktop result and a mobile result at the same time, updates them as you type, and flags titles or descriptions that are likely to be cut off with an ellipsis.

## Why preview your search snippet at all?

Your search result is a tiny advert competing with nine others. Ranking on page one is only half the job; the other half is earning the click. A title that ends in "…" just before the important word, or a description that trails off mid-sentence, wastes that chance.

Writing tags in a CMS field gives you no sense of how they will look. The preview puts them in context so you can make small edits, such as moving the keyword forward or trimming a filler phrase, that improve the result without changing the page itself.

## How does Google decide where to cut a title?

Google truncates titles and descriptions by **pixel width**, not by character count. On desktop the title area is roughly 600 px wide; descriptions get a wider area of around 920 px. On mobile the title can wrap to two lines, but the description has less room.

That is why "60 characters" is only a rule of thumb. Compare these two titles of similar length:

- "illustrated literary list of lit titles" is full of narrow letters.
- "WWW MEMBERSHIP MAXIMUM MOMENTUM" is full of wide ones.

The second takes far more space. The BISCS tool measures each title using the Arial font Google uses for results and shows the estimated width beside the character count, with a colour bar that turns amber near the limit and red when the title will be cut.

## How to use the Google SERP Preview tool

1. Open the [Google SERP Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/serp-preview/) and press **Sample** if you want to see a worked example first.
2. Type or paste your **Title**. Watch the counter show characters and approximate pixels.
3. Enter the page **URL**. The preview turns it into the breadcrumb-style path Google shows (for example, example.com › blog › seo-tips).
4. Paste your **Meta description**.
5. Add a **Focus keyword**. The preview bolds it in the description, the way Google often bolds matching words.
6. Optionally set a **Site name**, a custom **Breadcrumb** and a **Date** to see how a dated article result looks.
7. Compare the **Desktop preview** and **Mobile preview**, read the messages below the form, and edit until both look clean.

All of this happens in your browser. Your draft titles are not sent anywhere, which is useful when you are preparing pages for a launch that has not been announced.

## A checklist for a snippet that earns clicks

Use this list while you edit in the preview:

- **The topic comes first.** Put the words people search for at the start of the title, where they are least likely to be cut.
- **The title matches the page.** If you promise "Price List 2026" the page must have a current price list. Mismatches lead to quick back-clicks and Google rewriting your title.
- **The description answers "why this page?"** Mention what is inside, such as a calculator, a downloadable format or a comparison table.
- **Specific beats vague.** "Compare FD rates of 12 banks and calculate maturity in seconds" is stronger than "Best information about fixed deposits".
- **One brand mention is enough.** Add your brand name at the end of the title if space allows; do not repeat it in the description.
- **Readable on a phone.** Most searches in India happen on mobile, so check the mobile preview last and make sure the opening words still make sense.

## Common mistakes the preview helps you catch

**Titles that are too short.** A three-word title like "Home | Sharma Traders" wastes valuable space. Titles of 50–60 characters usually make the best use of it, and the tool nudges you when a title is under 30 characters.

**Descriptions that are too short.** If your description is very brief, Google is more likely to replace it with text pulled from the page, which may not be the part you would choose.

**Keyword missing from the title or description.** When you enter a focus keyword, the tool tells you if it is absent from either. That is not a ranking rule, but if the snippet does not mention what the person searched for, fewer people click.

**Long dated snippets.** When Google shows a date in front of a description, it uses up part of the space. Set the date field to see whether your description still fits.

**Broken URLs.** A typo in the URL field produces an error, which is a handy reminder to check the slug itself. Short, readable slugs such as `/gst-calculator/` look more trustworthy than `/index.php?id=4471`. The [Slug Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/slug-generator/) can help you make clean ones.

## Preview vs live result: what to expect

It helps to be clear about what any preview can and cannot do:

| | SERP preview | Live Google result |
|---|---|---|
| Title source | The title you typed | Usually your title tag, sometimes rewritten |
| Description | Your meta description | Your description or a passage chosen from the page |
| Truncation | Estimated from pixel widths | Actual rendering on the user's device |
| Extras | Optional date and breadcrumb | May add sitelinks, ratings, images or other features |

Google has publicly said it may rewrite titles that are too long, stuffed with keywords or do not describe the page. The best protection is simply a clear, honest title that fits.

## When to use it

Use the preview whenever you write or rewrite a title tag: new blog posts, product pages, service pages for local SEO in your city, or when you notice in Google Search Console that a page gets impressions but few clicks. Improving the snippet of a page that already ranks is often one of the quickest SEO wins available.

Once the snippet looks right, generate the full set of tags with the [Meta Tag Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/meta-tag-generator/), then check the published page with the [On-Page SEO Checker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/on-page-seo-checker/). Come back to the [Google SERP Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/serp-preview/) any time you test a new headline.

Q: What is the maximum title length for Google?
A: Google does not use a fixed character limit. It truncates titles by pixel width, roughly 600 pixels on desktop, which usually works out to about 50–60 characters. Narrow letters fit more, wide letters and capitals fit fewer, so checking the pixel width is more reliable than counting.

Q: Why is my search result different from the preview?
A: Google can rewrite titles and choose a different snippet from your page text, and its result design changes over time. The preview uses your own tags and Arial measurements, so treat it as a close guide to how your tags fit rather than a guarantee.

Q: Does Google bold my keyword in the snippet?
A: Google often bolds words in the snippet that match or closely relate to what the person searched for. The preview bolds the focus keyword you enter so you can see whether your description actually contains it in a natural way.

Q: Should I add a date to my meta description?
A: No, you do not type it into the description. Google may show a date before the snippet for articles, taking it from your page or structured data. The optional date field in the preview simply shows how much space that date would use.

## How to Sign a PDF Online for Free (Draw, Type or Upload)

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/sign-pdf-online-free-draw-signature/
Tool: Sign PDF (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/sign-pdf/)

Quick answer: To sign a PDF, open it in a signing tool, create your signature by drawing, typing or uploading a photo of it, place it on the signature line and download the file. BISCS India’s Sign PDF tool does all of this in your browser without uploading the document, which suits contracts, offer letters and forms.

To sign a PDF for free, open it in [Sign PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/sign-pdf/), click **Sign**, create your signature by drawing it, typing your name in a handwriting font or uploading a photo, then place it on the page and download. It takes under a minute, and the document never leaves your device.

Before you sign anything important, though, it is worth knowing what kind of signature the other side expects. A picture of your signature is fine for many purposes, but not all.

## Signature image, e-sign or DSC: which one do you need?

People use "e-sign" loosely, so here is a plain-language comparison. This is general information, not legal advice.

| Type | What it is | Typical uses |
|---|---|---|
| Signature image (drawn, typed or scanned) | A picture of your signature placed on the PDF | Offer letter acceptance, rent agreements between individuals, internal approvals, school and society forms, vendor quotations |
| Aadhaar eSign | An electronic signature issued through a licensed eSign service after Aadhaar-based authentication | Many online agreements and applications that ask specifically for eSign |
| Digital Signature Certificate (DSC) | A cryptographic certificate from a licensed Certifying Authority, usually on a USB token | Company law (MCA) filings, many tax and tender portals, documents that must be tamper-evident |

India's Information Technology Act, 2000 recognises electronic signatures, and the cryptographic kinds (DSC and eSign) can show who signed and whether the file changed after signing. A signature image cannot do that; it is evidence of intent, much like a scanned signed page.

So the practical rule is simple: **if the portal, bank, employer or authority asks for a DSC or eSign, a drawn signature will not do.** If they just ask you to "sign and send back", a signature image is usually what they mean. Some documents, such as wills and property sale deeds, have their own formalities, so take proper advice for those. When in doubt, ask the receiving party what they accept.

## How to sign a PDF step by step

1. Open [Sign PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/sign-pdf/) and choose the PDF you need to sign.
2. Click **Sign** in the toolbar. A signature window opens with three tabs.
3. Choose how to create your signature:
   - **Draw**: sign with your mouse, trackpad, finger or stylus, and pick an ink colour.
   - **Type**: type your name and choose one of four handwriting-style fonts.
   - **Upload**: add a photo or scan of your real signature; tick **Remove white background** for a clean result.
4. Confirm, then drag the signature onto the signature line and resize it from the corners.
5. Use **Add text** to type the date and place, and **Tick** for any checkboxes.
6. Scroll through all pages. Many agreements need a signature or initials on every page, so duplicate the signature (Ctrl+D) as needed.
7. Click **Apply & download** to save the signed copy.

## Tips for a signature that looks genuine

**Drawing on a phone is easier than with a mouse.** If you are on a laptop, consider opening the tool on your phone and signing with your finger, or use a stylus on a tablet.

**An uploaded signature looks most natural.** Sign on clean white paper with a blue or black gel pen, take a photo in daylight with no shadow, and upload it with background removal on. If you sign PDFs often, create a reusable transparent PNG once with the [Signature Maker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/signature-maker/).

**Keep the size realistic.** A signature that spills over the printed line or is tiny in a corner draws attention. Resize it to roughly match the space provided.

**Initials on every page.** For rent agreements and vendor contracts, it is common to initial each page. Create a second, smaller signature with just your initials.

## Common mistakes when signing PDFs

- **Signing the wrong version.** Check the date and the final clauses before signing. Once you send a signed PDF, it is hard to take back.
- **Using a signature image where a DSC is mandatory.** Government and company filings that require a DSC will reject a signed image.
- **Sharing your signature file casually.** A clean PNG of your signature is valuable. Do not post it in group chats or leave it in shared folders.
- **Forgetting the date.** Many documents are incomplete without the date and place next to the signature.
- **Signing a scanned page that is crooked.** If the document is a phone photo, clean it up first with [Scan to PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/scan-to-pdf/) so the final copy looks professional.

## A quick checklist before you hit download

- The signature sits on the correct line, on the correct page.
- Initials appear on every page if the document asks for them.
- The date, place and your printed name are filled in.
- No stray tick marks or test signatures are left on the page.
- You have kept the unsigned original, in case a correction is needed later.
- You know whether the receiver accepts a signature image, or needs a DSC or eSign instead.

## Office workflows: approvals and onboarding

Small offices often route purchase orders, leave forms and vendor quotations for a manager's signature. Instead of printing, signing and scanning, the approver can open the PDF, add their signature and the date, and send it back in a couple of minutes. HR teams can send offer letters as PDFs and ask candidates to sign and return them the same way.

For anything with a legal or regulatory requirement for a particular signature type, follow that requirement. For everything else, signing in the browser saves paper, printer trips and time.

## Is it safe to sign PDFs online?

With an upload-based website, your contract travels to someone else's server along with your signature. The BISCS tool works differently: the signing code runs inside your browser, the PDF is processed on your device, and nothing is uploaded. Signatures you create are held only for the current session.

Need to do more than sign? The full [Edit PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/pdf-editor/) tool adds whiteout, highlights, shapes and the ability to replace existing text, all with the same privacy.

Q: Is a drawn signature on a PDF legally valid in India?
A: It depends on the document and who receives it. Many offer letters, internal approvals and everyday agreements are accepted with a signature image. Some filings and documents need an electronic signature recognised under the IT Act, such as a Digital Signature Certificate or Aadhaar eSign. Check the requirement with the receiving party or a professional when in doubt.

Q: What is the difference between a signature image and a DSC?
A: A signature image is a picture of your handwriting placed on the page. A Digital Signature Certificate uses cryptography to prove who signed and that the file was not changed afterwards. A DSC is issued by a licensed Certifying Authority and usually lives on a USB token.

Q: Can I save my signature for next time?
A: During one session the tool remembers signatures you have created, so you can reuse them on several pages. It does not store them permanently. To reuse a signature later, keep a PNG of it on your device, or make one with the Signature Maker, and upload it when needed.

Q: How do I make an uploaded signature look clean?
A: Sign on plain white paper with a dark pen, photograph it in good daylight, and tick Remove white background when uploading. The tool trims the empty edges so the signature sits neatly on the line without a white box around it.

Q: Can I add the date and my name next to the signature?
A: Yes. The signing screen also has Add text and Tick tools, so you can type the date, your name, place or initials beside the signature before downloading the signed PDF.

## Social Share Preview: Check Link Cards for WhatsApp and LinkedIn

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/preview-link-whatsapp-facebook-linkedin/
Tool: Social Share Preview (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/social-share-preview/)

Quick answer: A social share preview shows how your link card will appear when someone shares the URL on WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn or X. BISCS India’s free Social Share Preview builds the cards from your title, description and image, checks the image size and ratio, and generates the Open Graph and X tags to paste into your page.

When you paste a link into WhatsApp or LinkedIn, the app fetches the page and builds a small card from its Open Graph tags: a title, a short description and an image. A social share preview lets you see that card before anyone else does, so you can fix a blurry image or a cut-off headline in advance.

The [Social Share Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/social-share-preview/) from BISCS India shows approximate cards for WhatsApp, Facebook, LinkedIn and X side by side, checks your image dimensions, and writes the tags you need.

## Why link previews matter so much in India

For many Indian businesses, WhatsApp is the main way links travel. A shop owner shares a festive offer page in customer groups, a college forwards an admission notice, a builder sends a project brochure link. If the card shows a grey box and a URL, it looks like spam. If it shows a crisp image and a clear headline, people tap it.

The same is true on LinkedIn for B2B services and on Facebook for local audiences. You only control these cards through a handful of meta tags, and you cannot see the result until someone shares the link, unless you preview it.

## Which tags control a link card?

- **og:title** is the headline on the card. If it is missing, apps fall back to your page title.
- **og:description** is the one or two lines under the headline. Not every app shows it.
- **og:image** is the picture. It must be a full `https://` URL.
- **og:url** and **og:site_name** tell apps the canonical address and your brand name.
- **twitter:card** set to `summary_large_image` tells X to show a big image card.

The tool generates all of these, and adds `og:image:width` and `og:image:height` once it has measured your image, which helps some apps render the card on the first share.

## How to preview and fix your link card

1. Open the [Social Share Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/social-share-preview/) and press **Sample** to see how a complete card looks.
2. Enter the **Title (og:title)** and **Description (og:description)**. Counters warn you when the title is likely to be cut off.
3. Add the **Page URL** and **Site name**.
4. Paste the **Image URL (og:image)**, or upload an image from your device just to try it out. Uploads stay in your browser and are never sent anywhere.
5. Read the image checks. The tool reports the pixel size and ratio, and warns if the image is too small, not 1.91:1, or large in file size for WhatsApp.
6. Compare the four previews. Pay attention to how the headline wraps and how the image is cropped.
7. Press **Copy** to get the Open Graph and X tags, and paste them into the `<head>` of your page.
8. After publishing, refresh any cached preview using the Facebook Sharing Debugger or LinkedIn Post Inspector.

## Getting the image right

The image does most of the work on a link card, and it is where most problems start.

| Check | Recommended | What goes wrong otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| Size | 1200 × 630 px | Below about 600 × 315 px, many apps show a small thumbnail instead |
| Ratio | 1.91:1 | Other shapes get cropped, often cutting off text |
| File size | As small as practical; under about 300 KB for WhatsApp | Heavy images are often skipped by WhatsApp |
| Format | JPG or PNG | Some apps do not support newer formats in previews |
| URL | Absolute `https://` address | Relative paths and `http://` images may not load |
| Content | Key text and logo near the centre | Edges are cropped in some layouts |

If your image is too heavy, shrink it with the [Image Compressor](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-compressor/). If it is the wrong shape, crop it to 1200 × 630 with the [Image Resizer](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/image-resizer/) before uploading it to your site.

## Common link preview mistakes

**Using the logo as the share image.** A square logo on a 1.91:1 card gets cropped or shrunk into a tiny thumbnail. Design a proper banner instead, with the logo as one element.

**Putting all the information in the image.** On some cards the title is overlaid or hidden. Keep the headline in og:title too, and use the image for visual impact.

**Same image on every page.** It is fine as a fallback, but your most-shared pages (offers, articles, product pages) deserve their own image so they are recognisable in a chat.

**Forgetting the cache.** Social networks remember previews. If you share a link before adding tags, the old blank card can stick for a while. Use the official debugging tools to refresh it.

**Blocking the crawler.** If your server or a security plugin blocks bots, apps cannot read your tags. Check that your robots.txt and firewall do not block social preview crawlers such as `facebookexternalhit`.

## Tips for headlines that work on small screens

Link cards are mostly read on phones, inside busy chats and feeds. A few habits help:

- Keep the headline to around 60–70 characters so it does not wrap awkwardly.
- Make the description concrete: what the reader will get, such as "Free checklist", "Prices from ₹499" or "Register by 15 December".
- Do not repeat the site name in the title if og:site_name already shows it.
- Write in the language your audience uses. A Bengali or Hindi headline for a regional audience is perfectly fine; just keep the text encoding as UTF-8.

## Approximate, not pixel-perfect

Each app changes its card design from time to time, and the cards in the tool are close approximations rather than screenshots. What they reliably show is whether your image loads, how it is cropped, and whether your text is likely to fit. That is enough to catch nearly every real-world problem.

For a full set of head tags, including the page title, description, robots and canonical tags, use the [Meta Tag Generator](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/meta-tag-generator/). Then come back to the [Social Share Preview](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/social-share-preview/) whenever you design a new share image or launch a campaign page.

Q: Why is my WhatsApp link preview not showing an image?
A: Common causes are a missing og:image tag, a relative image path instead of a full https URL, an image that is too large in file size, or a server that blocks the request. Compress the image, use an absolute https URL and test again in a new chat.

Q: What is the best Open Graph image size?
A: 1200 × 630 pixels, a ratio of about 1.91:1, works well across Facebook, LinkedIn, WhatsApp and X large cards. Keep text and logos near the centre because some apps crop the edges, and use JPG or PNG.

Q: I changed my og:image but Facebook still shows the old one. Why?
A: Social networks cache link previews. After updating your tags, use Facebook’s Sharing Debugger or LinkedIn’s Post Inspector to fetch the page again. WhatsApp also caches previews, so testing in a fresh chat may show the new card sooner.

Q: Is the image I upload to the preview tool published anywhere?
A: No. An uploaded image is only used locally to draw the preview in your browser. To make it appear in real link cards, you must upload it to your own website and paste its full URL into the image field.

Q: Do Open Graph tags help SEO?
A: They are not a Google ranking factor. Their value is in how your links look when shared, which affects how many people click them on social apps and messaging platforms. Google relies on your title tag and page content instead.

## How to Split a PDF by Page Ranges, Every N Pages or Singly

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/split-pdf-by-page-range-free/
Tool: Split PDF (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/split-pdf/)

Quick answer: To split a PDF, open a PDF splitter, choose how to divide it (page ranges such as 1-3, 4-6, fixed chunks of N pages, every page separately, or cut points you click), then download the parts as a ZIP. BISCS India’s Split PDF runs in your browser, so the document is never uploaded.

To split a PDF, open [Split PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/split-pdf/), choose a split mode and click **Split PDF**. You can split by page ranges (for example `1-3, 4-6, 7`), into chunks of a fixed size, into single pages, or by clicking the pages where each new file should start. The parts download together as a ZIP.

Pages are copied exactly as they are, so nothing is re-compressed, and the file is processed in your browser rather than uploaded to a server.

## Four ways to split a PDF

The tool offers four modes, and each suits a different job.

| Mode | How it works | Good for |
|---|---|---|
| Ranges | Type comma-separated ranges; each range becomes one PDF | Pulling chapters or sections apart |
| Every N | Cut the document into chunks of N pages | Monthly statements, batches for printing |
| All pages | Every page becomes its own PDF | Separating a bundle of single-page certificates |
| Pick | Click thumbnails; the file is cut after each selected page | Uneven sections you can spot visually |

The **Ranges** box is pre-filled with a sensible default (the first half and the second half), so you can see the format immediately.

## How to split a PDF step by step

1. Open [Split PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/split-pdf/) and choose your file.
2. Look at the page thumbnails to understand where each section starts and ends.
3. Pick a split mode: Ranges, Every N, All pages or Pick.
4. Enter your ranges or chunk size, or click the pages where you want cuts. The tool tells you how many files will be created.
5. Click **Split PDF**.
6. Download the ZIP and open it to find each part, named after the original file and the pages it contains.

## Real examples from everyday paperwork

**A combined scan from the office photocopier.** You scanned twelve documents in one go and got a single 30-page PDF. Use Pick mode: click the last page of each document, and you get twelve separate files.

**An annual bank statement.** Your bank emailed a 48-page PDF for the year, but the loan officer wants only the last six months. Use Ranges to split it into the two halves, or use [Extract PDF Pages](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/extract-pdf-pages/) to save just the pages you need.

**Exam answer sheets or certificates.** A school has a 40-page PDF with one certificate per student. "All pages" turns it into 40 files in seconds, ready to email individually.

**Printing in batches.** Large booklets are easier to print and staple in sets of 20. Every N with N set to 20 does it.

## Splitting to meet portal upload limits

Many Indian government and institutional portals cap the size of each upload, and the cap differs from portal to portal. If a scanned document is too big and the portal lets you upload several parts (some allow "Document 1", "Document 2" and so on), splitting is a clean solution.

Check the specific portal's instructions first. Some portals want a single file per document, in which case compressing is the better route. [Compress PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/compress-pdf/) can bring scanned files down considerably, and you can combine both approaches: split first, then compress any part that is still too large.

## Common mistakes to avoid

- **Overlapping or missing ranges.** If you type `1-5, 5-10`, page 5 appears in both files. If you type `1-4, 6-10`, page 5 is left out. The tool checks your input, but it cannot know your intention, so read the ranges once more.
- **Typing page numbers printed on the document.** Use the PDF's own page positions (as shown under the thumbnails), not the numbers printed in the footer, which often start after a cover page.
- **Splitting when you meant to remove pages.** If you only want to drop a few pages and keep one file, use [Remove PDF Pages](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/remove-pdf-pages/) instead.
- **Forgetting to rename the parts.** Names like `statement-pages-1-6.pdf` are clear, but a portal reviewer will appreciate `April-to-September-statement.pdf` even more.

## Tips for a smooth split

- An open-ended range such as `8-` runs from page 8 to the end, which saves counting.
- For very long PDFs, the Every N mode is quicker than typing many ranges.
- If the document has sideways pages, fix them first with [Rotate PDF](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/rotate-pdf/); split copies pages as they are.
- On phones, the ZIP lands in Downloads. Use your file manager to extract it before attaching parts to email or WhatsApp.

## Privacy and performance

The splitting is done by a PDF library that runs in your browser tab. Your file is read from your device and the parts are written back to your device, with no upload in between. That makes it suitable for medical reports, legal bundles and anything carrying Aadhaar or PAN details.

Because your own device does the work, a 500-page scanned PDF will take longer on a budget phone than on a desktop. The tool shows progress as each part is created, so you can see it working.

Q: How do I type page ranges for splitting?
A: Separate each part with a comma. For example 1-3, 4-6, 7 creates three files: pages one to three, pages four to six, and page seven alone. Each comma-separated range becomes its own PDF, and the file name includes the pages it contains.

Q: What is the difference between Split PDF and Extract PDF Pages?
A: Split PDF divides a document into several output files, usually covering all pages. Extract PDF Pages picks specific pages and saves them as one new PDF, or as separate files if you choose. Use split for breaking a big file apart and extract for pulling out a few pages.

Q: Why do I get a ZIP file?
A: Splitting usually produces several PDFs, and browsers handle one download better than many. The parts are packed into a ZIP that you can open on any phone or computer. On Android and iPhone, the Files app can extract it with a tap.

Q: Does splitting reduce quality or change the pages?
A: No. Pages are copied exactly as they are into the new files, so text stays selectable and images keep their original resolution. Each part’s file size is roughly proportional to the pages it contains.

Q: Can I split a scanned PDF?
A: Yes. Splitting works on pages, not on text, so scanned and digital PDFs both split the same way. Scanned pages are often large, so if a part is still too big for an upload portal, compress it afterwards.

## Free Word Counter: Count Words, Characters and Reading Time

URL: https://www.biscsindia.com/blog/word-counter-characters-reading-time/
Tool: Word Counter (https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/word-counter/)

Quick answer: To count words, paste or type your text into a word counter and read the totals instantly. BISCS India’s free Word Counter shows words, characters with and without spaces, sentences, paragraphs, reading and speaking time, plus keyword density, all in your browser without saving or uploading your text.

A word counter tells you exactly how long your text is: the number of words, characters, sentences and paragraphs, and roughly how long it takes to read or say out loud. Paste your text into the box and the numbers update as you type.

That sounds simple, but the count is often the thing standing between you and a rejected application, a cut-off caption or an essay that loses marks for being too long. Here is how to use one well, and what the different numbers actually mean.

## What does a word counter actually count?

The [Word Counter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/word-counter/) on BISCS India shows ten figures at once:

- **Words**: every word-like unit, counted with language-aware rules.
- **Characters**: everything you typed, including spaces and line breaks.
- **Characters without spaces**: useful for some form fields and translation quotes.
- **Sentences** and **paragraphs** (a paragraph is any block separated by a blank line).
- **Lines** that contain text.
- **Reading time** at about 200 words per minute and **speaking time** at about 130.
- **Unique words** and **average word length**, handy for spotting repetition.

Below the totals there is a **keyword density** table listing your 12 most frequent words with their count and percentage. Common filler words such as "the", "and", "का" and "है" are skipped so the list shows the words that carry meaning.

## How to count words online, step by step

1. Open the [Word Counter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/word-counter/) in any browser, on a phone or computer.
2. Paste your text into the large box, or start typing. You can also press **Sample** to see how it works.
3. Read the totals in the stats panel. They update as you type, so you can trim and watch the numbers fall.
4. Scroll down to the keyword density table if you want to check for overused words.
5. Press **Copy** to copy your edited text back out, or **Clear** to start again.

There is nothing to install and no sign-up. Your text stays on your device because the counting runs inside the page itself.

## When does an exact count matter?

Plenty of everyday tasks in India come with a hard limit. A few common ones:

- **College and scholarship essays**: statements of purpose often specify a range such as 500 to 800 words. Going over can look like you ignored instructions.
- **Board exam and university answers**: practising to a target length helps you plan time in the exam hall.
- **Job application forms**: "Describe yourself in 150 words" boxes on careers portals sometimes cut off text silently.
- **Social media**: X (formerly Twitter) has a 280-character limit for standard posts at the time of writing, and Instagram captions are capped at 2,200 characters. Limits change, so treat these as guides.
- **Web pages**: search engines shorten long titles and meta descriptions in results, so writers aim for roughly 50 to 60 characters for titles and 150 to 160 for descriptions.
- **Freelance writing and translation**: many clients pay per word, so both sides need an agreed count.

## Word count vs character count: which one should you use?

It depends on who sets the limit. This quick table helps.

| Situation | Usually measured in | Tip |
|---|---|---|
| Essays, SOPs, articles | Words | Ask whether headings and references are included |
| Social posts, SMS, ads | Characters (with spaces) | Leave a 5–10 character margin |
| Form fields on websites | Characters | Some forms count line breaks as two characters |
| Translation quotes | Words or characters without spaces | Confirm the unit before quoting a price |
| Speeches and voice-overs | Speaking time | Rehearse aloud; the estimate is a starting point |

## Why do different tools give different counts?

You may notice that Microsoft Word, Google Docs and online counters disagree by a few words. That is normal, because each one has its own rules for edge cases:

- **Hyphenated words** like "well-known" or "co-operative" may be one word or two.
- **Numbers and symbols** such as "₹5,000" or "10%" may or may not count as words.
- **Emoji and Indic text** can be counted as one character or several, depending on how the tool handles Unicode.
- **URLs and email addresses** are sometimes split at every dot.

The BISCS counter uses the browser's built-in text segmentation, which follows international Unicode rules. That is why Hindi, Bengali or Tamil words, and characters like "क्ष", are counted as you would expect rather than being split into pieces. If you are submitting to a portal that has its own counter, always check the final count there as well.

## How to use keyword density without overdoing it

The keyword table is useful for two different jobs.

For **writers and students**, it reveals habits. If "very", "basically" or your main subject appears far more than anything else, you probably need synonyms or tighter sentences.

For **bloggers and small businesses**, it shows whether your main topic actually comes through. A page about "GST registration" should mention the phrase naturally, but there is no magic percentage. Search engines reward pages that answer the question clearly, and repeating a phrase unnaturally can make the page read worse. For a deeper on-page look, try the [Keyword Density Checker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/keyword-density-checker/), and pair it with the [Readability Checker](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/readability-checker/) to see whether your sentences are easy to follow.

## Common mistakes when working to a word limit

- **Counting the wrong text.** Check whether the title, headings, footnotes and bibliography count towards the limit before you trim.
- **Pasting from a PDF.** Text copied from PDFs often carries broken lines and doubled spaces that inflate paragraph and line counts. Run it through the [Whitespace Cleaner](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/whitespace-cleaner/) first.
- **Trusting reading time blindly.** Technical notes, legal text and content in a second language take longer to read than 200 words per minute.
- **Cutting meaning to save words.** Remove repetition, filler and long introductions before you remove examples.
- **Ignoring the platform's own count.** Social apps and online forms may count emoji, links or line breaks differently from any external tool.

## Practical tips for trimming text quickly

If you are 50 to 100 words over, look for these first:

- Phrases like "in order to" (use "to"), "due to the fact that" (use "because") and "at this point in time" (use "now").
- Sentences that start with "It is important to note that". Usually the rest of the sentence stands alone.
- Repeated summaries at the start and end of each paragraph.
- Lists of three examples where two would do.

When you need to change the style of your text rather than its length, the [Case Converter](https://www.biscsindia.com/tools/case-converter/) can quickly fix headings typed in capitals.

## Is it safe to paste confidential text?

Yes, as far as this tool is concerned. The Word Counter runs entirely in your browser. Your draft is not uploaded, logged or saved by BISCS India, which matters when you are counting an unpublished manuscript, a legal document or an answer you have not submitted yet. Closing the tab clears it.

As with any website, avoid pasting passwords or banking details into text boxes you do not need to, and use your own device rather than a shared cyber café computer for sensitive work.

Q: Do word counters count hyphenated words as one word or two?
A: Most tools, including the BISCS Word Counter, follow standard word-boundary rules, so a term like well-known is usually split into two words. Microsoft Word treats it as one. If an exact count matters for a submission, check which tool the examiner or editor uses and follow that.

Q: Does the word counter work for Hindi, Bengali and other Indian languages?
A: Yes. The tool uses your browser’s built-in language-aware text segmentation, so words written in Devanagari, Bengali, Tamil and other scripts are counted properly, and conjunct letters are not broken apart when counting characters. Sentences ending in the Hindi full stop (purna viram) are also recognised.

Q: How is reading time calculated?
A: Reading time divides your word count by about 200 words per minute, a typical silent reading speed for adults. Speaking time uses about 130 words per minute, closer to a comfortable presentation pace. Treat both as estimates, since technical text and nervous speakers both run slower.

Q: Is my text stored anywhere when I use the counter?
A: No. The counting happens in JavaScript inside your browser tab. Your text is not sent to a server or saved by BISCS India, and it disappears when you close or clear the page, so it is fine for unpublished drafts, answers and confidential documents.

Q: Why does my character count differ from what an app shows?
A: Apps count differently. Some count emoji or accented letters as two characters, some ignore line breaks, and some shorten links. The BISCS counter counts visible characters including spaces and line breaks. For strict limits, leave a small margin and check the final post in the app itself.
